bank_theme: Albania — POS acceptance mandate + deposit-ATM growth
signal: MOVED THIS CYCLE: the acceptance estate is now measured at the central bank rather than the trade association. Bank of Albania's own terminal series puts POS at **38,662 at end-Q2-2026** (38,615 EFTPOS plus 47 cash-advance), up from 32,224 at end-Q1-2026, 31,263 at end-2025 and 24,481 at end-2024 — **+23.7% in six months and +57.9% over eighteen months**, with roughly 10,700 terminals added in twelve months and virtual POS at 389 (A4, A6). H1-2026 card payments at POS were 16,006,404 transactions worth ALL 58.3bn, and card payments at POS have now stably overtaken ATM cash withdrawals at about 56 of every 100 card operations (A4, A6). The driver is legal, not commercial: the Law on Tax Procedures as amended by Parliament at end-2025 obliges businesses to hold a terminal during 2026, with accommodation, transport and public enterprises bound from **end-May 2026** and the remainder by **31/12/2026**, inside a national cashless-by-2030 objective (A6). Running alongside it, the POSi National Electronic Payments Acceleration Programme — a government, Albanian Association of Banks and Mastercard scheme launched 27/03/2025, not a Mastercard-only offer — now has **five confirmed acquirers: Raiffeisen, Union Bank, BKT, Credins and OTP Albania**, giving a free terminal and 0% commission for twelve months up to EUR 20,000 a year, and **valid until 31/12/2026 or until all terminals are distributed** (A1). Caution carried from the source: 38,662 terminals is about 28% of Albania's ~138,000 active enterprises, but many terminals sit inside chains, so it is not 28% of businesses (A6). Two acquirers are actively substituting software for hardware — Raiffeisen offers RaiPOS softPOS plus a free NFC smartphone as an alternative to a terminal (A1).

bank_theme: Albania — TIPS Clone instant-payment rail, November 2026 go-live
signal: The single dated event in this market. Banca d'Italia announced on **20/07/2026** that its TIPS Clone instant-payment settlement platform went live for the Western Balkans, that Bosnia and Montenegro joined first, and that **a second onboarding window is scheduled for November 2026 when the central banks of Albania, Kosovo and North Macedonia are expected to join** (A3, primary). Governor Gent Sejko then said at the 05/08/2026 monetary-policy briefing that the project is in its closing implementation phase and the system should be fully operational **within November 2026, at the latest by end-November**, quantifying savings at up to ALL 35bn a year for the financial system and ALL 38bn for the economy (A3 and A5, multi-outlet). Bank of Albania's own National Payment System Committee minutes of 16/12/2025 confirm the programme and record Banca d'Italia's original **July 2026** target, so the November date is a slip (A4, primary). Two design features matter commercially: transfers addressable by **mobile phone number instead of IBAN**, and a **Verification-of-Payee check** that the account belongs to the named payee before the payer confirms (A4). The platform settles in local currency in central-bank money and in euro in commercial-bank money — two separately screened flows (A3). Context volumes: SEPA credit transfers went live 07/10/2025 and AIPS-EURO customer payments rose from 31,545 in January to 49,005 in July 2026, while the AECH retail clearing house hit a record 237,974 transactions in July alone, +46.2% in seven months (A4); AIPS, AIPS-EURO and AECH were all moved to ISO 20022 during 2025 (A4). CAVEAT: there is no Bank of Albania press release, no day-level date and **no published commercial-bank participation list or bank-side legal deadline** — this is Governor-driven urgency, not a statutory obligation on banks (A3, A5).

bank_theme: Printec Albania / Bank of Albania banknote-machine certification — the fitness gate
signal: Bank of Albania's official list of **customer-operated** banknote-handling machines tested for the lek contains only **two entries, and Printec Albania Ltd is the named distributor for both**: the NCR SelfServ 6682/6684/6632/6634 family (tested 20/02/2026) and the LIVIX 7 from Vivex Group Belgrade (tested 30/01/2026). The staff-operated list is almost entirely fitness-capable and is held by Giesecke+Devrient, Cima and Italdes units distributed by **Mellon Albania and Pelikani Security; Printec appears nowhere on it** (A4, list dated 10/07/2026). bank_theme: Albania — branch counter cash and paper payments, the teller-automation case
signal: Bank of Albania's own forms quantify how much cash and paper still crosses the counter. **Over-the-counter cash transactions in H1-2026 were 3,357,815 items worth ALL 1,170.8bn**, of which counter cash **deposits alone were 2,279,914 items worth ALL 783.7bn** — against ATM deposits of 1,378,900 items worth ALL 68.6bn over the same half-year, so **the branch counter absorbs 11.4 times the cash-deposit value the entire ATM estate does**, and businesses are 73% of counter deposit value (A4). In parallel, **paper-based credit transfers still ran at 3,250,200 items worth ALL 2,477.9bn in H1-2026 — 33.1% of customer transfers by count but 62.1% by value**, with business paper transfers alone worth ALL 1,612.1bn (A4). The estate this lands on is growing, not shrinking: **408 bank branches at end-2025, up from 400, the highest since 2021, with about 46% in Tirana** (A4, press reporting of central-bank data). Cash outside banks reached ALL 505.7bn at June-2026, +4.6% in six months and +14.4% year on year on the central bank's own annual-change line, so note volume is rising in absolute terms even as card acceptance explodes (A4). ProCredit Albania states the underlying economics plainly to its own customers: staffed counters open roughly 30 hours a week against 24/7 self-service zones, deposits credited in under five minutes, and a night-safe tier for businesses depositing over ALL 1,000,000 a day (A1).

bank_theme: Albania — eIDAS2 electronic identification and digital identity wallet law adopted
signal: The Albanian Parliament **adopted on 07/05/2026, after committee review on 4-5 May, the law "On electronic identification, trusted services and the digital identity wallet", stated to be fully aligned with the EU eIDAS and eIDAS2 regulations**. It creates a digital identity wallet provided free to citizens that can store and prove identity data and electronic attestations of attributes, sign and seal documents electronically, log every digital interaction and work offline and cross-border; it widens the range of qualified and non-qualified trust services and hardens supervision of eID schemes, wallets and trust-service providers (A4, national cyber-security authority announcement 14/05/2026). This closes a gap the European Commission had flagged: its Albania Report of 04/11/2025 stated verbatim that Albania should adopt such a law to align with the European Digital Identity regulation, confirming that as of late 2025 no eIDAS-aligned law existed (A3). Implementing acts are still pending and the accreditation route for qualified trust-service providers is not yet published (A4).

bank_theme: Austrian competitor landscape — Loomis pushing automated cash, Worldline retreating, no Payten presence
signal: Three vendor movements reported this cycle change the competitive picture in Austria. Loomis published its half-year report on 24/07/2026 showing Q2 revenue of SEK 7,891m against SEK 7,407m, currency-adjusted growth of 9.1%, and a record operating margin of 14.0% against 12.7%, which the chief executive attributes to strength in the International and Automated Solutions lines — Automated Solutions being Loomis's cash-recycling and smart-safe hardware-and-service business, the direct rival to Printec's teller cash recycler proposition, and Loomis Oesterreich GmbH is in the footprint. Worldline moved the other way: its bank-facing Financial Services division fell 7.1% organically in H1-2026 to EUR 363m with margin down about 300 basis points, the chief financial officer quantified a EUR 60m full-year 2026 drag from CONTRACT TERMINATIONS of which half was booked in H1, and the chief executive said the division will not return to growth before the second half of 2027; the company is also cutting Western European headcount at a guided 4–5% a year through 2030, with Austria touched through PAYONE and the former SIX Payment Services book. No client names or geographies were disclosed for the terminations. Third, ASEE's half-year subsidiary schedule shows the group has NO registered operating entity in Austria, so Payten has no local delivery presence there — though the group's Romanian, Croatian and Turkish entities can and do sell across borders, so this is absence of local delivery, not inability to compete.
date: 30/07/2026 — Worldline H1 results confirming the EUR 60m termination drag; Loomis H1 results 24/07/2026; ASEE entity schedule 31/07/2026
implies: The three point the same way. Banks are terminating legacy Worldline processing and ATM-management contracts at a EUR 60m-a-year run rate and Worldline itself says the division will not grow again before H2-2027, so outsourced bank estates are coming back to market for at least six more quarters — and a vendor removing 4–5% of its Western European staff every year is a vendor whose local field-engineering depth is under strain, which is exactly the ground Printec wins on. Against that, Loomis is converting its cash-in-transit relationships into recycler-and-smart-safe managed services faster than its transport base is growing, so the Austrian commercial recycler opportunity is contested from the cash-logistics side rather than from the ATM side. And bid teams in Vienna should stop pricing against a Payten shadow on local-presence assumptions, while still watching for a Payten acquisition as the entry route.
likelihood: Likely that at least one footprint bank re-tenders Worldline-run services within twelve months; Loomis pressure is ongoing
follow_up: Identify by name which Austrian banks use Worldline Financial Services processing or ATM management, particularly through the former SIX Payment Services book, and diary their renewal windows; ask contacts whether termination notices have already been served. Get Glory and Sesami recycler proposals in front of Austrian banks and retailers before Loomis converts its cash-in-transit relationships. Re-read Worldline's Q3 release on 27/10/2026 for the remaining EUR 30m of the termination drag.

bank_theme: Finanzmarktaufsicht (FMA) — the regulator itself is a biddable buyer for analytics and security tooling
signal: Correcting an earlier read, the FMA does run open, above-EU-threshold, published-value competitive procedures for supervisory analytics and security tooling, and they draw very few bids. Its "Analysetool Kryptowaehrung" cryptocurrency-analytics tool went to SoftwareONE Oesterreich GmbH at EUR 126,121.68, contract concluded 12/03/2026 for a 365-day term by OPEN procedure above threshold, on ONE offer received, FMA file 3601.05055. The same pattern holds for its co-managed round-the-clock security operations centre, awarded to Arrow ECS GmbH at EUR 385,600.00, concluded 26/11/2025 by open procedure above threshold for a three-year term, again on one offer, FMA file 3601.04801. Other FMA buys on the portal over the last twelve months include a Splunk security-monitoring subscription renewal on 18/06/2026, Palo Alto intrusion-prevention maintenance, a web-application firewall renewal, Microsoft Azure and Copilot, a data-governance subscription on 09/04/2026, a low-code platform, business-process consultancy, and an Atos requisition for NIS2 services dated 30/07/2025. One open tender is live, "FMA-Standort — Management- und Unterstuetzungsleistungen", published 21/08/2026 and closing 02/10/2026, but that is facilities management and not addressable.

sources.text: USP eProcurement — FMA Analysetool Kryptowaehrung award

date: 18/06/2026 — most recent FMA security-tooling award on the portal; crypto-analytics award concluded 12/03/2026; live facilities tender closes 02/10/2026
implies: This flips the earlier conclusion that the regulator was a relationship-only account. Single-bid open procedures are the softest targets there are, and the subject matter — crypto-asset analytics, security monitoring, anti-money-laundering-adjacent tooling — sits directly on Printec's compliance and financial-crime line. SoftwareONE and Arrow ECS are resellers and integrators rather than regulatory-technology product owners, so partnering through them is a live route into the account rather than a blocker. Note that FMA's NIS2 work already sits with Atos, so that specific door is closed.
likelihood: Further open above-threshold FMA analytics and security procedures within twelve months on the observed cadence
follow_up: Register on the Austrian USP notifier for CPV 48000000 and 79417000 filtered to FMA. Approach SoftwareONE Oesterreich and Arrow ECS as reseller routes for the anti-money-laundering and financial-crime product line into the FMA.

bank_theme: Oesterreichische Nationalbank — security-technology maintenance bridge expires 31/12/2026
signal: A contract modification notice, TED 157688-2026 published 06/03/2026, extends OeNB's maintenance of security technology and of security doors and airlocks — parts II and III of reference IGImmo/006-5, CPV 50610000 — by three months, modifying an award originally made under TED 338405-2019. The winner is PKE Electronics GmbH at EUR 357,589.26, with the contract concluded 03/03/2026 and no subcontracting. The decisive detail is in the notice text: the existing service contract, which had been running to 31/08/2026, is extended to 31/12/2026. The recorded justification is that only the incumbent can perform the work because it developed the entire security-management software and all the interfaces between subsystems, and that the modification stays under the 50% ceiling in section 365(3)(5) of the Austrian procurement act. Procurement is handled through IG Immobilien Management GmbH, represented by DORDA Rechtsanwaelte. See NOTES — a second agent could not corroborate this from the link it was given.
date: 31/12/2026 — the extended maintenance contract expires, so a replacement procurement or a further extension must surface in autumn 2026
implies: The central bank's physical-security estate is locked to PKE Electronics because PKE owns the security-management software and every interface into it, and OeNB has now bought itself a bridge that runs out at the end of 2026. That gives a dated window: any replacement procurement has to appear during autumn 2026 or the bridge has to be extended again. The subject matter is adjacent to Printec's physical ATM security line, but the software ownership makes displacement hard, so the re-tender is realistically the only entry point — and its timing is now known.
likelihood: A re-tender or a further extension must appear before 31/12/2026
follow_up: Watch the Austrian USP portal and TED before 31/12/2026 for an OeNB "Wartung Sicherheitstechnik" procedure, and approach IG Immobilien Management, which runs the procurement, ahead of it. Re-source the PKE award through a browser session on the Austrian portal to close the corroboration gap before the name is used in any customer-facing material.

bank_theme: Erste Bank Oesterreich and Raiffeisen Bankengruppe join EPI — Wero comes to Austria
signal: RBI announced on 22/06/2026 that Erste Bank Oesterreich and the Raiffeisen Bankengruppe — RBI itself plus Raiffeisenlandesbank Niederoesterreich-Wien, Raiffeisenlandesbank Oberoesterreich and Raiffeisen-Landesbank Steiermark — will join the European Payments Initiative as new shareholders and make the Wero account-to-account payment scheme available to Austrian customers. This is explicitly conditional: the release states it is subject to the respective supervisory boards' approval. Wero is put at more than 55 million users, live in Germany, Belgium and France, with Luxembourg planned for 2026 and the Netherlands for 2027, and Austria's roughly nine million residents described as a strategic growth market. No Austrian consumer go-live date was disclosed.

sources.text: RBI — EPI begruesst Erste Bank Oesterreich, Raiffeisen Bank International und Raiffeisen Landesbanken als neue Anteilseigner

date: 22/06/2026 — Austria's two largest banking groups announce they will join EPI, subject to supervisory-board approval; no go-live date published
implies: Wero is a scheme that moves money directly between bank accounts and bypasses the card rails. Taking it to merchants means acceptance-side work: point-of-sale and terminal software updates, QR and dynamic acceptance flows, merchant onboarding, and a second authorisation path running alongside cards. For Printec's point-of-sale and acquiring lines that is a scheme migration of the same class as a chip-card or instant-payments rollout. But this must be treated as a preparation-phase signal, not a funded programme — the shareholding itself is still pending supervisory-board approval and no Austrian go-live date exists. Any suggestion that RBI will extend Wero acceptance into its CEE subsidiaries is inference, not something RBI has said.
likelihood: Medium — Austrian launch preparation is plausible within 6–12 months, but the shareholding is still conditional and no go-live date is disclosed
follow_up: Confirm that the supervisory-board approvals actually completed, and track the announcement of an Austrian Wero launch date, which is the point at which acceptance-side budget commits. Test separately whether RBI intends to extend Wero acceptance into CEE, rather than assuming it.

bank_theme: Austria — EUDI Wallet will miss end-2026 on the responsible minister's own record
signal: Confirmed verbatim at the parliamentary record: in the National Council Budget Committee on 29/06/2026, State Secretary for Digitalisation Alexander Proell said that not a single EU member state will have implemented the EU Digital Identity Wallet requirements by the end of 2026, and that around 6 million ID Austria identities have already been activated. Federal Chancellery budget figures were confirmed at EUR 652.6m for 2027, an increase of EUR 103.5m, and EUR 660.5m for 2028, with digitalisation up EUR 39.9m in 2027. A parliamentary answer on the introduction of the EU Digital Identity Wallet, 5687/AB of 12/08/2026 from Interior Minister Gerhard Karner, is confirmed to exist, though the characterisation that the questions fall outside the interior ministry's remit sits inside the answer PDF and has not been re-read verbatim. Austria's building blocks remain ID Austria and the eAusweise app.
date: 24/12/2026 — relying-party registration duty applies; derived wallet-acceptance date remains 24/12/2027; ministerial statement 29/06/2026
implies: Austria will reach the end of 2026 with a partial, incrementally delivered wallet built on ID Austria and eAusweise rather than a certified EU wallet, and the responsible State Secretary has said so on the record. That shifts rather than removes the opportunity: the bank-side duties are not suspended because a national provider slips, relying-party registration still applies from 24/12/2026, and the derived acceptance date stays 24/12/2027 — so Austrian banks face a compressed 2027 integration window. The sellable position is a wallet-agnostic acceptance layer that works against ID Austria and eAusweise now and against a certified wallet later, combining remote identity verification, relying-party middleware and hardware-based key protection. Budget commits in H1-2027.
likelihood: High — stated on the record by the responsible State Secretary in committee
follow_up: Retrieve the 5687/AB answer PDF and confirm its wording before any of it goes into a customer-facing deck. Track the Austrian e-government and electronic-identity law amendments that will designate the wallet provider, the national certification scheme and the conformity assessment body, and ask the FMA or OeNB whether anything has been said to banks about relying-party registration.

bank_theme: Bosnia & Herzegovina — IPS BiH mandatory participation (rulebook 10/07/2026, deadline 01/01/2027)
signal: The domestic instant-payment rail went live on 20/07/2026 with three banks and has already grown to five: Nova banka a.d. Banja Luka joined on 28/07/2026 and ATOS Bank a.d. Banja Luka on 17/08/2026, both Republika Srpska banks, so roughly 16 of BiH's 21-22 licensed banks are still outside the scheme (A1, A3, A4, A5). Two things moved materially this cycle. First, a full read of the CBBiH rulebook uncovered Article 7(2), a ROLLING trigger the master row missed: any bank exceeding 500,000 cumulative real-time-gross-settlement and giro-clearing transactions in a calendar year must become a participant from 1 July of the following year, so the addressable set widens every year rather than closing on 01/01/2027 (A3). Second, Article 15 tightens the engineering envelope well beyond what the master row recorded — maximum execution time for an instant payment is 5 SECONDS, with a 7-second scheme timeout and a 10-second hard timeout, so fraud and sanctions screening must clear inside roughly five seconds, not ten (A3). Article 13 still makes a mobile or electronic-banking app the only permitted way to start a payment, caps a single order at BAM 5,000, and reserves QR-code initiation to a CBBiH specification that has still not been published (A3, A4). The underlying platform is independently confirmed as Banca d'Italia's TIPS Clone, live 20/07/2026 with BiH and Montenegro as the first two central banks aboard and a second onboarding window in November 2026 for Albania, Kosovo and North Macedonia (A3).

sources.text: CBBiH — Odluka o pravilima rada sistema instant plaćanja

date: 17/08/2026 — ATOS Bank becomes the fifth participant · 01/01/2027 statutory participation date for every bank over the one-million-transaction test · rolling 500,000-transaction trigger each 1 July thereafter
implies: About sixteen banks must, inside four months, build what most do not have: ISO 20022 payment-message connectivity (the international standard for payment messages), a working mobile or e-banking app because the rulebook allows no other way to start a payment, fraud and anti-money-laundering screening that finishes inside five seconds, hardware security modules and key management, and round-the-clock liquidity monitoring. The central bank's joiner announcements are a free, dated pipeline tracker that can be polled monthly to time each approach. Publication of the QR specification opens a second wave of card-acceptance and merchant work on top of the initial connection.
likelihood: Certain — the rulebook is in force and 01/01/2027 falls inside the window
follow_up: Obtain CBBiH's H1-2026 RTGS and giro transaction counts to name exactly which banks crossed the one-million test and are therefore bound to 01/01/2027, and the calendar-year counts feeding the rolling 500,000 trigger. Establish which integrator built the Nova banka and ATOS gateways, since that firm becomes the default for the remaining Republika Srpska banks. Register for the CBBiH QR specification on publication. Poll the participant page monthly.

bank_theme: Bosnia & Herzegovina — SEPA accession + ISO 20022 structured-address remediation
signal: The application is now actually filed. On **06/08/2026 CBBiH formally submitted BiH's application to join the Single Euro Payments Area**, closing a two-year programme run through the SEPA Accession Coordination Board that CBBiH chairs alongside both entity finance ministries, both banking agencies and the BiH Banking Association; a draft had been lodged 12/12/2025 and the last precondition fell on 28/07/2026 when the FBiH House of Representatives adopted the harmonised financial laws the Republika Srpska National Assembly had already passed (A1, A4). The European Payments Council is now reviewing the file. CBBiH states explicitly that commercial banks must align their IT and business systems with SEPA standards and join the relevant European payment schemes, that a significant part of that work can only be done AFTER formal admission, and that the first SEPA transactions can be expected at the earliest six months after admission — so the six-month post-admission clock, not the application, is the sales trigger (A1, A4). The World Bank estimates BiH fee savings of around EUR 100m and CBBiH notes BiH does over 80% of its foreign trade with SEPA countries (A4). Two domestic message-format facts were confirmed from primary gazette and central-bank text this cycle. CBBiH's giro-clearing system already uses the SEPA message format conforming to ISO 20022 and to whichever European Payments Council rulebook version the central bank designates as current — so the 14-15/11/2026 SWIFT SR2026 removal of unstructured postal addresses reaches BiH retail clearing the moment that designation carries it, and that designation is not publicly dated (A3). Meanwhile BiH high-value RTGS is still legally pinned to SWIFT MT formats (MT102, MT103, MT202, MT205 with mandatory service code BAP), with the Governor empowered to set the switch to ISO 20022 pacs.008 and pacs.009 on only **fifteen days' written notice** once all participants are ready — the shortest lead time to a live cutover anywhere in the footprint (A3).

sources.text: CBBiH — "CBBiH zvanično aplicirala za pristupanje SEPA području"

date: 06/08/2026 — CBBiH files the official SEPA application, EPC review under way · 14-15/11/2026 SWIFT SR2026 structured-address cut, inherited domestically the moment CBBiH designates a 2025-or-later EPC rulebook · RTGS ISO 20022 cutover undated, 15 days' notice
implies: A 21-bank IBAN, ISO 20022, credit-transfer and direct-debit migration with sanctions and politically-exposed-person screening upgrades and structured party-data remediation has moved from lobbying to execution. BiH banks have small in-house change capacity and buy externally. Because the Governor's RTGS trigger is "all participants ready", every laggard bank sits on the critical path, which makes a readiness assessment sellable to the slowest banks and to CBBiH itself — and fifteen days is far too short to start selling after the notice lands, so position now. No membership timetable and no published contract value exist, so no size band is invented here.
likelihood: High that admission proceeds; membership timing not officially stated; the November-2026 address cut is fixed
follow_up: Ask CBBiH Payment Systems which EPC rulebook version is currently designated as current for giro-clearing internal credit payments — that single answer decides whether the 15/11/2026 structured-address cut bites domestically, and it remains the highest-value unanswered question in BiH. Monitor the CBBiH register of regulations and Službeni glasnik BiH for the Governor's RTGS MX notice. Obtain the FBiH and RS payment-services law texts for hard compliance dates. Screen the 21 banks for absent ISO 20022-native payment hubs.

bank_theme: Bosnia & Herzegovina — bank modernization + FATF grey-list
signal: The estate is now visible bank by bank rather than as a market total. FBA preliminary data at 30/06/2026 (published 13/08/2026) name every FBiH-headquartered bank's fleet: Raiffeisen 359 ATMs and 9,824 POS, UniCredit d.d. Mostar 265 and 11,131, Sparkasse 123 and 0, Intesa Sanpaolo 117 and 2,355, ASA Banka 100 and 1,042, NLB Sarajevo 91 and 2,912, BBI 91 and 0, Addiko Sarajevo 75 and 0, ZiraatBank 74 and 1,570, ProCredit 35 and 0, Privredna banka Sarajevo 32 and 0, Union banka 32 and 0, KIB Velika Kladuša 6 and 0 — 1,400 ATMs and 28,834 POS in total (A1, A4). ABRS at the same date shows Republika Srpska-headquartered banks at 490 ATMs and 12,483 POS, up from 478 and 10,168 at 31/12/2025 (A1, A4). The single most commercially useful new number is the CBBiH device-type split for 2025: of 1,868 installed ATMs, 1,281 are dispense-only, 567 take cash in, and only 20 do bill payment — deposit-capable machines jumped from 345 to 567 in one year, a 64% rise, while dispense-only fell slightly and **bill-payment ATMs were cut from 128 to 20** (A4). Cash in circulation outside banks rose 8.56% to KM 7.46bn in 2025 against a branch network frozen at exactly 749 units for two years running (A4). Republika Srpska is roughly twice as cash-intensive as the Federation: 20.0% of RS payment transactions by count are still cash against 9.5% in FBiH (A1). BiH's FATF grey-listing of **19/06/2026** is now confirmed on a primary regulator source, FBA's own statement of the same day, which stresses the causes sit outside banking and that effects on international banking business are limited (A1, A3, A4).

sources.text: CBBiH — Kartičarstvo u BiH u 2025. godini

date: 13/08/2026 — FBA publishes bank-level ATM and POS fleets at 30/06/2026 · 19/06/2026 FATF grey-listing confirmed on FBA's own statement · 11/03/2026 CBBiH publishes the deposit-capable split
implies: A dated, quantified replacement cycle is already running: 222 machines converted to cash-accepting in a single year, with 1,281 dispense-only units still to convert, at a market where the branch count is frozen and physical cash volume is rising. That is the textbook case for cash recyclers — machines that re-dispense the notes customers deposit, cutting cash-in-transit runs. The bank-level table turns this from market sizing into account planning: four banks hold 864 of the 1,400 Federation ATMs. Read the bill-payment collapse as a warning, not an opening — BiH banks deployed payment kiosks, the mobile app took the journeys, and the fleet was withdrawn, so any kiosk pitch must beat a demonstrated in-market failure. Lead cash automation with Republika Srpska banks, where one payment in five is still cash.
likelihood: High — conversion already running at over 200 units a year and the regulators refresh the numbers quarterly
follow_up: Ask each of the 13 FBiH and 8 RS banks which of their cash-accepting ATMs are true recyclers rather than deposit-only, since the CBBiH category does not distinguish. Target the 1,281 remaining dispense-only units. Pull the final FBA Q2-2026 report due around September or October 2026 to firm the provisional figures. Ask banks that retired the 108 bill-payment ATMs what failed, before pitching any kiosk.

bank_theme: Payten / Asseco SEE — BiH ATM service incumbency and a disclosed retreat
signal: Printec's closest regional rival holds most of the BiH ATM estate under service and has just disclosed that its BiH business is shrinking. Payten states it maintains approximately **1,200 ATMs in Bosnia & Herzegovina** including Diebold Nixdorf and NCR machines, and that it is the only provider in BiH servicing all global ATM brands — roughly two-thirds of the CBBiH national count of 1,868, though the claim is five-year-old vendor copy dated 2020-2021 (A4). The most material lock-in is a **long-term ATM outsourcing agreement signed 28/09/2021 between Payten BiH and Intesa Sanpaolo Banka BiH**, covering ATM application deployment on Diebold Nixdorf machines, network monitoring through Payten's ProView software and maintenance; Intesa holds 117 ATMs and is one of the five IPS BiH banks. Payten also migrated 90-plus Banqit ATMs at Sparkasse Bank BiH to Diebold Nixdorf and supplied Diebold Nixdorf machines to Sparkasse and MF Banka (A4). The new, dated development is ASEE Group's H1-2026 report of 31/07/2026, which puts the Payment Solutions segment at EUR 102.8m, down 5% year on year, and attributes the ATM-line fall of EUR 3.4m "primarily from lower equipment deliveries in South-Eastern Europe, particularly in Serbia, Croatia, **Bosnia and Herzegovina** and Montenegro", with Q2 worse again on the same countries (A6). The country table makes BiH the standout: **BiH revenue EUR 16.4m, down 5%, and BiH EBIT EUR 2.8m, down 20% — the only footprint country going backwards on both lines** while Serbia grew 13% and North Macedonia 29% (A6). Payten's order backlog shows contracted revenue flat to down while contracted margin rises, the disclosed pattern of a firm taking fewer, better-priced deals (A6).

sources.text: ASEE Group — Management Report on Operations for the six months ended 30 June 2026

date: 31/07/2026 — ASEE H1-2026 report discloses falling BiH ATM deliveries, BiH revenue -5% and BiH EBIT -20% · 26/10/2026 Q3 update is the next reading
implies: Entry into BiH ATM services is displacement, not greenfield, and the target is specific: Payten's moat is the bundle of ATM application software, ProView monitoring and maintenance at named banks, so the attack is multivendor ATM software that runs the estate regardless of whose hardware it is, plus telemetry and managed-service commitments at contract renewal. The 567-and-growing cash-accepting conversion is the wedge that does not require displacing a service contract at all, because it is new-capability spend competing on cash-handling economics rather than incumbency. The backlog shape suggests Payten will hold price to defend margin this autumn rather than undercut, which makes late 2026 the moment to test firm pricing. Note that Payten is not leaving payments — it is trading box sales for recurring service revenue — so the credible attack is on hardware refresh and estate modernisation, not on the whole relationship.
likelihood: Medium — displacement depends on renewal timing and the Intesa agreement is "long-term" with no published end date
follow_up: Establish Payten's service-contract renewal dates bank by bank, starting with Intesa Sanpaolo Banka BiH. Confirm whether the 1,200-ATM figure is still current from ASEE investor relations or the segment note in its annual report, since it is five-year-old marketing copy. Re-read the Q3-2026 report on 26/10/2026 to see whether the BiH ATM line recovers or the retreat is structural. Watch whether Payten's Monri multi-acquirer single-terminal model, which already has a Sarajevo legal entity, is pushed into BiH merchant acceptance.

bank_theme: FBiH Banking Agency — binding ICT-risk decision with an annual external ICT audit due 31/03/2027
signal: BiH banks are the regulated island in an unregulated country, and the rulebook now has a hard filing date. FBA's binding "Odluka o upravljanju informaciono-komunikacionim sistemom i IKT rizikom u banci" was adopted 25/02/2025 and has been **in application since 31/12/2025**; it is BiH's equivalent of the EU's operational-resilience regime and mandates measures to protect the cryptographic keys that encrypt data at rest and in transit, ICT incident and cyber-threat reporting to FBA, resilience testing, third-party oversight, and both internal and external ICT audit. **The external ICT-system audit report is a standalone report every bank must deliver to FBA no later than 31 March of each year — next 31/03/2027, applying to all 13 FBiH banks** (A4). Sitting on top of it, FBA's supervisory expectations for 2026, published 20/02/2026, require penetration testing and red-team exercises, layered security controls, data encryption, network segmentation, continuous monitoring, automated attack response, continuity plans covering rebuilding systems from zero, a full register of every outsourced activity with direct board accountability, and transaction-monitoring systems tuned to actual BiH client behaviour including cash flows, diaspora remittances and cross-border payments (A1, A4). Banks are already acting: **three of the largest FBiH banks resolved at their spring-2026 AGMs to commission external audits** — UniCredit Bank d.d. Mostar appointed KPMG for a financial-statement audit including an assessment of AML obligations plus a separate information-system audit, ASA Banka resolved to select an external ICT auditor, and NLB Banka d.d. Sarajevo appointed an auditor across three separate scopes covering financial statements, the AML segment and the ICT system. Those three banks hold 447 of the Federation's 1,400 ATMs and 15,085 of its 28,834 POS terminals (A1).

sources.text: FBA — Supervizorska očekivanja u vezi sa postupanjem banaka u 2026. godini

date: 31/03/2027 — statutory deadline for every FBiH bank to file its external ICT-system audit report with FBA, recurring annually · 30/06/2026 three large banks confirm AGM-mandated ICT and AML audits · 31/12/2025 the ICT-risk decision entered into application
implies: A named, auditable compliance lane across all 13 Federation banks, with the Republika Srpska banks facing a parallel ABRS rule. The explicit cryptographic-key requirement maps directly to hardware security modules and remote key injection — loading ATM and POS encryption keys over the network instead of sending two custodians to every device. The resilience-testing and outsourcing-register requirements map to managed services with contractual service levels and device telemetry, and the board-accountability wording means the buyer is the board rather than IT. The BiH-tuned transaction-monitoring requirement maps to real-time monitoring and screening. The 31/03/2027 filing is the calendar hook: audit fieldwork runs Q4-2026 into Q1-2027, findings land in Q1 and budget follows, so positioning has to happen now.
likelihood: High — the decision is already in force and the audit filing recurs every 31 March
follow_up: Obtain the ABRS equivalent ICT decision covering the 8 Republika Srpska banks. Work backwards from 31/03/2027 and position key management, remote key injection and telemetry during Q4-2026 fieldwork. Scan the remaining BiH banks' 2026 AGM agendas — published in every bank's regulatory filing — for the same ICT and AML audit resolutions, identify the appointed auditors, and time approaches to each post-audit remediation window. Confirm the FBiH gazette reference for the ICT decision.

bank_theme: Seven FBiH banks with zero own POS estate — greenfield card acceptance
signal: The regulator's own bank-level table exposes a clean structural gap: at 30/06/2026 **seven of the thirteen FBiH-headquartered banks report ZERO POS terminals of their own** — Sparkasse (123 ATMs), BBI (91), Addiko Sarajevo (75), ProCredit (35), Privredna banka Sarajevo (32), Union banka (32) and KIB Velika Kladuša (6). They issue cards but do not acquire, so merchant acceptance is either outsourced or absent, which makes any terminal, terminal-management or software-POS pitch greenfield rather than a displacement fight (A1, A4). Sparkasse is the most interesting of the seven: 123 ATMs against only 46 branches and sub-branches makes it comparatively self-service-heavy, it is one of only three IPS BiH launch banks which signals genuine payments-investment appetite, and its ATM fleet was migrated to Diebold Nixdorf by Payten in 2018-19 (A1, A4). The demand side is moving fast underneath them: card acceptance is expanding far quicker than the ATM count across BiH, with POS up 3,079 units in six months against 30 more ATMs, and Republika Srpska POS growing 23.5% year on year against 4.5% in the Federation (A1, A4). BiH-wide there were 37,895 POS terminals at end-2025, 215 million card transactions in 2025 at an average of KM 98, and 70% of card transactions are already contactless (A4).

date: 13/08/2026 — FBA publishes the bank-level POS table at 30/06/2026 showing seven banks at zero · same-date ABRS data show RS POS growth of 23.5% year on year

bank_theme: UniCredit Bank d.d. Mostar — largest FBiH acquirer, fresh funding, two mandated audits, not yet on the instant rail
signal: The bank's H1-2026 regulatory filing, signed 31/07/2026, shows total assets of KM 9.298bn up from KM 8.753bn at the start of the year, pre-tax profit KM 112.4m against KM 106.0m a year earlier, 1,125 employees and 69 branches (A1). Three things make it a live account rather than a large one. First, **KM 100.1m of issued debt instruments now sits on the balance sheet where there was nothing on 01/01/2026**, following a second bond issue approved at an extraordinary shareholder meeting on 11/05/2026 and earmarked for lending growth and the regulatory loss-absorbing-capacity requirement. Second, the March 2026 AGM mandated KPMG both to audit the bank's AML and counter-terrorist-financing obligations and, separately, to audit the bank's information system for 2026, and adopted the 2025 IT-governance audit report — two remediation streams running simultaneously. Third, **intangible assets fell to KM 10.45m from KM 12.97m**, meaning software capitalisation is running below amortisation, which says a refresh is due rather than in progress (A1). It holds **265 ATMs and 11,131 POS terminals, the largest card-acceptance estate in the Federation**, alongside a further 99 UniCredit retail branches disclosed at group level for BiH split between Banja Luka and Mostar (A1, A4). It is **not yet an IPS BiH participant**, so the instant-payment integration and the SEPA work are both still ahead of it (A1, A3).

What the portal is genuinely useful for is postal and utility cash handling, and it produced three dated results this cycle. Hrvatska pošta d.o.o. Mostar awarded a **framework agreement for cash-in-transit, premises guarding and alarm monitoring worth BAM 697,000 excluding VAT against a BAM 700,000 estimate — 99.6% of the ceiling on a SINGLE BID — to a consortium of SEC ONE d.o.o. and Delta Security d.o.o., running 20/07/2026 to 20/08/2028**, award notice published 19/08/2026 (A2, A6). JP BH Pošta awarded **13 banknote-counting machines to SALON BANKARSKE OPREME d.o.o. for BAM 50,310 excluding VAT on a one-year contract concluded 19/06/2026**, with two bids received but only one acceptable, so the requirement recurs around June 2027 (A2, A6). And **Pošte Srpske a.d. Banja Luka tried twice in 2025 to buy money-counting machines and a vacuum banknote counter and cancelled both attempts** — an unmet, twice-failed cash-counting requirement still sitting open (A2). CBBiH's only visible 2026 procurement was a money-museum fit-out, awarded to ABV Sistem for BAM 294,450 — no central-bank banknote-processing or ATM procurement was published at all (A2).

bank_theme: BAMCARD d.d. Sarajevo — the domestic processor, and an unresolved partner-or-compete question

It has also launched a cardless ATM withdrawal service for microcredit disbursements with Partner MKF and ASA Banka, and a dynamic currency conversion service certified by Visa and Mastercard. Two things are unresolved and matter. First, **BAMCARD makes no public claim to be involved in IPS BiH or in CBBiH's planned QR scheme**, so whether it builds the participant-side gateways for joining banks — and is therefore the partner or the competitor on the largest opportunity in this market — is not established. Second, a **"Notice of Acquisition of the Company's Shares" dated 23/09/2025 under the FBiH Takeover Law** sits unexplained on its news page, so it is not known whether control has changed. CBBiH data separately show BAMCARD-branded cards are accepted at only four banks' ATMs and one bank's POS, so its own acceptance footprint is narrow (A1). Its careers page returned a 404 on 31/08/2026, so no hiring signal could be read (A5).

bank_theme: Bosnia & Herzegovina — no electronic-identity or trust-services law, remote onboarding legally blocked
signal: The European Commission's BiH 2025 Report states verbatim, in the financial-services section, that **"There is no legal and regulatory framework for digital identity, and banks can only offer hybrid solutions"**, and in the digital chapter that **"No progress was made in adopting a Law on electronic identity and trust services for electronic transactions in line with the EU acquis"**, that the recommendation to establish a single countrywide supervisory body remains, and that there was no progress on interoperability of electronic signature across the country (A3, A4). Both quotations were confirmed word for word this cycle. The state-level draft law remains with the Council of Ministers and is not adopted. A set of press-tier claims about a Republika Srpska entity law on electronic identification said to have been adopted in June 2026, a March 2026 Constitutional Court finding, and a June 2026 letter from the IDDEEA director **could NOT be verified this cycle and must not be presented as fact** (A3). The Commission separately told BiH to set up a countrywide beneficial-ownership register — still not done, and a named FATF action-plan item — and to align with the payment-services and e-money directives and the SEPA regulation, which is now done in both entities (A4).

sources.text: European Commission — Bosnia and Herzegovina 2025 Report, SWD(2025) 751 final

date: STANDING: 04/11/2025 — EC BiH 2025 Report confirms no e-identity or trust-services law; the EC's 2026 enlargement package, expected around October or November 2026, will re-score it
implies: This closes the remote-identity question in the negative on a primary source, and it cuts both ways. A fully remote, identity-only onboarding product cannot be sold as compliant in BiH this cycle and should not be put on a roadmap. But because identity cannot be proven remotely, the physical channel stays load-bearing — which is a positive for branch and self-service lines: assisted-onboarding stations, cash-accepting and recycling ATMs, and electronic signature deployed in an attended rather than unattended configuration. The adjacent gap is that BiH still has no network-and-information-security law at all, while FBA has already imposed resilience rules on banks, so banks are regulated ahead of the country. The beneficial-ownership register, a FATF action-plan item, is a separate data-quality opening.
likelihood: Medium — the law has been recommended repeatedly and not adopted; SEPA and FATF pressure is the new forcing function
follow_up: Watch for the EC's 2026 BiH report around October or November 2026 and for any draft state law on electronic identity and trust services. Source the claimed June-2026 Republika Srpska entity law in the RS official gazette and the March-2026 Constitutional Court decision before either is used commercially. Ask CBBiH and both banking agencies which identification method they will accept for remote account opening.

bank_theme: Bulgaria — post-euro changeover consolidation
signal: The changeover is now formally closed by the regulator and the calendar is fully dated. BNB Governor Dimitar Radev published a seven-month retrospective on 21/08/2026 stating "the technical transition is complete, the real work continues", and confirmed Bulgarian banks now draw Eurosystem liquidity on common terms (A3). The statutory dual lev-euro price display ended on **08/08/2026** under ZVERB Art.15(2) as amended, and three banks have already cut over their channels — UniCredit Bulbank from 09/08/2026, UBB and the KBC companies in stages from 12/08/2026, Postbank from 14/08/2026 (A1, A5). Critically for the device estate, ZVERB Art.21(2) item 3 required dual-currency amounts on **ATM cash-withdrawal screens only during that display period**, so that obligation fell away on 09/08/2026 and every Bulgarian ATM and kiosk estate now needs a screen and receipt reversion release (A3). The residual lev tail is quantified: BGN 29.4bn exchanged and 94.48% of lev cash withdrawn by 30/06/2026 with **BGN 1.7bn still outside BNB vaults**, against EUR 8.8bn of euro cash in circulation; free exchange ended at banks on 30/06/2026 but UBB and UniCredit Bulbank both extended it voluntarily to **30/09/2026**, banks may not refuse the service until **31/12/2026** and may discontinue it only from 01/01/2027 after pre-notifying BNB under Ordinance No.47 Art.2(4) (A1, A3). Consumer-protection enforcement did not stop — it changed legal basis: KZP and the revenue agency ran 37,955 euro-related inspections to 13/08/2026 with EUR 3.26m of penalties, and the ban on unjustified price rises runs on under the Consumer Protection Act to 09/08/2027 (A3).

sources.text: evroto.bg — BNB Governor Radev, seven-month assessment (BG)

date: 21/08/2026 — BNB Governor declares the technical changeover complete; dual display ended 08/08/2026 and the ATM-screen dual-display duty fell away 09/08/2026; free exchange ends at UBB and UniCredit Bulbank 30/09/2026; statutory duty to exchange ends 31/12/2026
implies: The budget freeze is over. Bulgarian bank IT and cash budgets locked on changeover delivery through H1-2026 are released into the 2027 planning round that is being set right now, in September to November 2026. Three concrete pieces of paid work fall out of the dates: a screen and receipt reversion release across every ATM and self-service estate now that dual display is redundant, the retirement of lev validator profiles, firmware and cash-forecasting parameters once the exchange duty ends on 31/12/2026, and a single-currency re-baselining of cash forecasting and cash-in-transit routing on a fleet that has never run a full euro year. Pitch this as post-changeover optimisation, not changeover support.
likelihood: High — every date is statutory and fixed, and the 2027 budget round is open now
follow_up: Open the Q4-2026 conversation at DSK, UBB, Postbank, UniCredit Bulbank and Fibank on two bundled items — the post-08/08/2026 ATM and kiosk screen reversion release, and lev decommissioning plus single-currency cash-forecast re-baselining. Ask BNB's Issue Department for the Ordinance 47 list of banks that have notified an exchange fee or a discontinuation date: those banks are furthest through the wind-down and are the first to need re-optimisation.

bank_theme: Bulgaria — big-four ATM estate: deposit-capability white space quantified
signal: The white space has now been re-measured on a **single synchronised date, 27/08/2026**, from each bank's own live locator feed, and it has barely moved in a month. **UBB**: 737 ATM pins, 244 with the cash-deposit feature, so 493 dispense-only (33% deposit-capable), against 738 and 246 on 30/07/2026 — flat. **Postbank**: 668 location records, 501 ATM-tagged, 226 deposit-capable, so 275 dispense-only; the estate grew by three ATM sites in four weeks and the deposit-capable share did not move (45.2% to 45.1%), meaning **new machines are still going in dispense-only** — the strongest available evidence that no recycler decision has been taken. **DSK**: 724 ATM-bearing sites of 777 records, with only 214 carrying either deposit tag and just 133 carrying the explicit deposit-ATM tag, so between roughly **510 and 620 sites are cash-out-only**; in 169 of 285 localities not one site takes a deposit. **UniCredit Bulbank**: 761 ATM records, only 197 deposit-capable, so 564 machines (74.1%) are cash-out only (A1). Two new reconciliations sharpen the sizing: OTP's H1-2026 statutory report puts DSK at **952 ATMs** at 30/06/2026 against 724 ATM-bearing sites, so at least 228 machines sit above one-per-site — pins are locations, not terminals (A1). bank_theme: Bulgaria — Verification of Payee cliff at 01/01/2027 (legal basis contested)
signal: **THE CONTESTED LEGAL BASIS IS NOW RESOLVED, AND THE ATM ESTATE IS EXPLICITLY IN SCOPE.** The carried verification debt was closed this cycle against the Official Journal text itself: Regulation (EU) No 260/2012 Article 16(9), inserted by Article 1(5) of the Instant Payments Regulation (EU) 2024/886, provides that where the euro is introduced in a Member State before 09/04/2027 its payment service providers must comply with Articles 5a, 5b and 5c **within one year of euro introduction**. Bulgaria adopted the euro on 01/01/2026, so the obligation bites on **01/01/2027** — it is directly applicable EU law, not a regulator assertion, and the previously feared 09/01/2027 non-euro date is irrelevant here (A3). The decisive new detail for Printec: **recital 11 of Regulation 2024/886 names the initiation channels expressly — "online banking, a mobile application, an automated teller machine, a self-service terminal, in a branch or by phone" — and requires no difference between instant and other credit transfers across channels**, while ZVERB §1 item 16 defines a Bulgarian ATM as a device that also executes transfers between payment accounts. The ATM and kiosk estate is therefore inside VoP scope as a matter of primary EU text, not inference (A3). UBB went live with VoP on 15/07/2026 with four match outcomes, 24/7, stating the same 01/01/2027 market obligation (A1); BORICA's VoP service has run live since October 2025 and is certified by the European Payments Council as a Qualified Routing and Verification Mechanism (A2, A6).

bank_theme: Bulgaria — European Accessibility Act market surveillance now bites on ATMs and payment terminals

The dated change is that a transitional provision halved all Chapter Six penalties for infringements committed up to 01/06/2026, so **full rates have applied since that date** — BGN 1,000 to 5,000 on individuals or BGN 5,000 to 25,000 on undertakings, doubling on repeat breach. bank_theme: Croatia — free-basic-services package: deposit-migration driver with a coin carve-out
signal: The statutory basis is now nailed down, closing the master row's open question. The instrument is the Act amending the law on comparability of fees, payment-account switching and access to a basic account, published in the official gazette Narodne novine 105/2025 on 23/07/2025 (A5). From 01/01/2026 any consumer receiving regular income into a payment account may REQUEST a free basic package covering account opening and maintenance, internet or mobile banking at the bank's choice, cash DEPOSITS at counters or ATMs excluding coin processing, cash withdrawals at the account bank's own counters or ATMs, incoming transfers, and issuance and use of a debit card at physical points of sale. From 01/01/2027 package holders and vulnerable basic-account holders may additionally withdraw cash TWICE A MONTH FREE OF CHARGE at ANY OTHER Croatian bank's ATMs. The Ministry of Finance question-and-answer document of 04/02/2026 confirms the coin carve-out verbatim, and the bank's response deadline fell from 30 days to 10 working days on 02/07/2026. Take-up remains small: 108,171 packages against 5.9m consumer accounts, or 1.6%. Nationally there are only 45 coin-deposit machines (A1). CONTRADICTION RESOLVED: one A1 row this cycle cautioned that the 01/01/2027 cash-access right "could not be substantiated" — it is substantiated, by the gazette citation and the Ministry press release, and by the Government's own statement (A2).

bank_theme: Croatia — European Accessibility Act (NN 89/2025): the harshest fines in the footprint, with the central bank as supervisor of bank services
signal: Croatia's transposition of the European Accessibility Act was adopted on 06/06/2025 and published in the official gazette Narodne novine 89/2025 on 13/06/2025, entering into force on 28/06/2025. Verified in the gazette text (A3): it covers self-service terminals including ATMs, payment terminals, ticketing machines and interactive information terminals; market surveillance of those products sits with the State Inspectorate, while surveillance of CONSUMER BANKING SERVICES sits with the CROATIAN NATIONAL BANK and the financial-services supervisor, each within its competence. The penalties are the highest of the five transpositions checked this cycle: a manufacturer that is a legal person faces EUR 6,630 to EUR 132,720 for placing on the market a product not designed to the accessibility requirements, and the SAME band applies to a SERVICE PROVIDER that fails to make its service accessible — an order of magnitude above Cyprus, Romania and Bulgaria. Service providers have until 28/06/2030, and self-service terminals lawfully in use before 28/06/2025 may run to the end of their economic life but no more than TWENTY YEARS from entry into use. An annex example requires literally "fitting a socket and installing software on the ATM to allow headphones to be connected so that on-screen text is reproduced as sound", alongside text-to-speech, multi-sensory time-out warnings, time extension, contrast, tactile key distinguishability and no requirement of high force. No enforcement decision against any bank or terminal had been published as at 27/08/2026.

What it buys is ATMs with the audio socket and screen-reader stack the annex literally describes, accessibility retrofits where the chassis allows, multivendor ATM software so one compliant accessible interface can be delivered across a mixed-manufacturer estate, accessible PIN pads with remote software push to merchant estates, and above all an estate audit that establishes each machine's twenty-year clock. Budget commits in 2028-2029 for a 2030 estate, so the audit and roadmap are what sell now — and the absence of any enforcement action so far is exactly the pre-enforcement window in which readiness sells.

bank_theme: Cyprus — a direct-sales market, not a tender market, with the Housing Finance Corporation the one public bank buyer
signal: A documented zero, and it is a coverage finding as much as a commercial one. Across this cycle no open or awarded Cypriot public notice exists for ATMs or ATM software, recyclers, self-service or branch kiosks, POS terminals or terminal management, softPOS, instant payments, transaction-monitoring or fraud systems, key-management hardware or ATM physical security. The reason is structural: the commercial banks are private companies and therefore not contracting authorities, so their buying never reaches the portal or the EU journal, and the Central Bank of Cyprus procures entirely outside the national portal under its own directives, publishing in the Official Gazette and on its own site and reaching the EU journal only above threshold — then DELETING closed notices, so its sub-threshold pipeline is invisible after the fact (A2). The exception is the state-owned Housing Finance Corporation, the only Cypriot bank that is a contracting authority. It awarded project-management services to Deloitte Limited at EUR 648,520 against a EUR 650,000 estimate on a SINGLE bid, award date 10/07/2026, after the notice had to be published four times; and it paid Pansophic Software EUR 13,800, uncontested and without prior call for competition, to migrate its property valuation system out of KEDIPES' data centres — evidence both that the run-off vehicle for the former co-operative bank book is being unwound and its shared IT re-homed, and that a credible bidder can win at this buyer with no competitive pressure at all (A2, A6). Adjacent public cash-handling demand exists outside the banks: the Electricity Authority's banknote-counter tender at a EUR 55,000 estimate drew four bids — TH.K. Office Supplies at EUR 31,400, Mastertype C.P. Services at EUR 33,000, A. Finiris at EUR 43,600 and Brink's Cyprus at EUR 59,050 — and has sat under evaluation for ten and a half months; and the central bank's SWIFT gateway administration contract went to Allied Engineering Group (Cyprus) at EUR 415,000 on a single bid.

bank_theme: Cyprus accessibility law — a 28/06/2030 replacement cliff for every ATM and payment terminal
signal: Cyprus transposed the European Accessibility Act by the Accessibility of Products and Services Law N.57(I)/2024, gazetted on 02/05/2024, and the primary Greek legal text was read directly this cycle to close a carried verification debt. It applies to products placed on the market from 28/06/2025 and names self-service terminals expressly, including payment terminals and ATMs, ticketing machines, check-in machines and interactive information terminals. Section 45 gives a transitional period ending 28/06/2030 during which a service provider may keep using products it lawfully used before that date, with pre-28/06/2025 service contracts able to run to expiry but never beyond five years — a hard replacement cliff for the installed estate. The competent authority is the Deputy Minister of Social Welfare, NOT the central bank and not the consumer-protection service, and the Council of Ministers has still not published the decision designating the accessibility surveillance authorities, so the enforcement layer remains a live gap. Administrative fines are low at EUR 10,000, or EUR 20,000 for a repeat breach, but the criminal provision runs to two years' imprisonment on first conviction and three on a second (A3).

sources.text: CyLaw — N.57(I)/2024 Accessibility of Products and Services Law

date: STANDING: 02/05/2024 — law gazetted; obligations bite for products placed on the market from 28/06/2025 and the transitional period for the existing estate ends 28/06/2030
implies: Every Cypriot bank faces a dated obligation to make ATMs and payment terminals accessible — audio output, tactile keypads, screen reader or voice guidance, reach and contrast — and an accessibility audit is a no-regrets opening that can be led with rather than waited for, particularly at Eurobank Limited where only SOME machines carry embossed keys or headphone ports. Sell the 2030 replacement cliff plus procurement-clause and board-level criminal exposure, not fine avoidance, since the administrative ceilings are trivial. bank_theme: Cyprus acceptance market — softPOS erodes terminal supply while Mellon takes full local control
signal: Physical card acceptance in Cyprus is being re-terminalised in software rather than hardware. Business acceptance of mobile payments jumped from 36% in 2024 to 68% in 2026 while card acceptance stayed broadly flat at 88%, and cards are 75% of all non-cash payment volume, the highest share in the euro area (A5). Viva.com will self-supply the ENTIRE public-service terminal estate on Tap-on-Any-Device software under the state contract, and payabl., a Limassol e-money institution, launched its own Tap to Pay softPOS on Android in March 2026 with iOS support stated for later in the year — a second Cypriot provider crossing from online acquiring into in-person acceptance without shipping a terminal (A6). At the same time Mellon Technologies completed the buy-out of the remaining 45% of Mellon Cyprus Ltd on 24/06/2026, making it wholly owned — the same pattern the group ran in Croatia, Slovenia and Hungary, and normally the prelude to putting a country under direct group control and pushing the full catalogue through it. Payten and ASEE, by contrast, have NO registered operating entity in Cyprus, so the local rivals are Mellon, Euronet, the softPOS providers and local integrators rather than Payten — though a Cypriot acquisition would be Payten's obvious entry route. The central bank raised the barrier to new entrants from 03/08/2026: a mandatory pre-application stage carrying a non-refundable EUR 5,000 fee, the licence application fee doubled from EUR 5,000 to EUR 10,000, a power to require an externally prepared enhanced due-diligence report, and automatic withdrawal of inactive applications (A5, A6).

bank_theme: Czech banks — instant euro payments and Verification of Payee, on a fixed 2027 clock
signal: The Czech National Bank confirms on its own instant-payments page, re-read 27/08/2026, that from January 2027 Czech banks must be able to RECEIVE instant euro payments and from July 2027 also to SEND them around the clock — and, commercially the decisive point, states in its own words that THE SYSTEM FOR INSTANT EURO PAYMENTS IS NOT OPERATED BY THE CNB and has nothing to do with participation in CERTIS. Every Czech bank must therefore procure its own euro instant reachability and stack (A3). The underlying legal text was re-read and a previous mis-dating reversed: under Regulation (EU) 2024/886 the calendar for non-euro member states is 09/01/2027 banks must receive instant euro transfers and meet the charges-parity rule, 09/04/2027 e-money and payment institutions must receive, and 09/07/2027 all providers must SEND and must offer Verification of Payee — the payee-name-against-IBAN match — free of charge (A3). Domestic koruna instant payments are already mainstream, at nearly 43.6 million payments through CERTIS in June 2026 and about 46.4% of all interbank transfers in April 2026 against 21% in mid-2022, but bulk payments and standing orders are EXCLUDED today, and the CNB is working to add bulk instant payments in 2026 — a separate second integration (A3). bank_theme: Greece — IRIS instant payments as a mandated card alternative
signal: The cross-border phase went live and it created a named competitive gap the master row did not capture. On 30/06/2026 the first phase of IRIS Payments' European interconnection went live for person-to-person transfers covering 57.3 million citizens in five countries, delivered through the Greek clearing operator DIAS joining the EuroPA alliance, which links the Greek, Portuguese, Spanish and Italian account-to-account schemes so users send by mobile number with no account number. Reach is expected to expand to more than 176 million citizens in 18 European countries BY END-2026, and from 2027 interoperability is planned to extend to payments at electronic and physical stores. The material detail: the service is initially available ONLY THROUGH EUROBANK, PIRAEUS AND VIVA.COM — ALPHA BANK AND NBG ARE THE NAMED GAP, with the remaining Greek banks expected to join in the period ahead (A3). Volume context from the clearing operator's own 2025 statistics: instant payments 122.1m transactions, up 72.8% and 27% of all credit transfers; person-to-person IRIS 111.4m transactions, up 90%, with 4.3m registered users; professional IRIS up 197% across 583,445 registered professionals; commerce IRIS up 70.8%. Interbank ATM transactions ALSO rose 27.7% in 2025, but that print covers under five months of the zero-fee withdrawal regime, so 2026 will be the first full year (A1). DIAS is separately working to roll commerce IRIS into physical stores through a per-transaction QR code shown on the terminal (A1). Cardlink and Worldline dominate Greek public-sector card acceptance, so the terminal decision sits with the acquirer, not the buyer (A2, A6).
date: 30/06/2026 — IRIS goes live cross-border through the EuroPA alliance with only Eurobank, Piraeus and Viva participating; expansion to 18 countries expected by end-2026; merchant and retail interoperability slated for 2027
implies: Two sharper angles than before. Immediately, Alpha and NBG are confirmed NOT on the cross-border scheme while three rivals are — a named, dated onboarding gap to sell into ahead of the end-2026 scaling event. From 2027, cross-border account-to-account acceptance at Greek merchants means QR and alias acceptance across the terminal estate, terminal-management changes and merchant onboarding — a software and management refresh across an installed base rather than a terminal-sale driver — alongside rising demand for real-time fraud monitoring on a rail that bypasses cards entirely. Meanwhile interbank ATM usage is GROWING fast, which cuts the other way and supports the cash-automation and ATM managed-services case.
likelihood: High for the end-2026 expansion; Medium for the 2027 merchant leg, which is press-only
follow_up: Approach Alpha and NBG on their cross-border onboarding timelines now, while they are the named laggards. Pitch IRIS and QR acceptance plus terminal management onto the installed terminal fleets rather than new terminals, and position instant-payment fraud monitoring to the four systemics and to DIAS. Obtain the DIAS and EuroPA primary roadmap documents — the end-2026 and 2027 dates are press-only — and separately source the IRIS transaction-limit changes and the mandatory-acceptance rule, neither of which is in the cited article.

bank_theme: Greece — softPOS / Tap-to-Pay commoditises card acceptance
signal: The competitive price and feature walls in Greek card acceptance are now documented line by line from live vendor pages. Worldline's Greek Tap to Pay on iPhone offer — card acceptance in a phone app with no terminal hardware, live since 27/05/2025 — carries a published price of €24.19 plus VAT for one year or €44.35 for two, at 1.15% on Greek and European cards plus €0.05 per transaction; alongside it Cardlink and Worldline bundle card acceptance with the tax-authority-certified fiscal cash-register function in a single device sold through the Eurobank network (A6). Mellon's competing merchant shop sells terminals bundled with NBG Pay acquiring from €159 plus €3.50 a month excluding VAT for a countertop unit, or €79 down and €7 a month on lease, with no softPOS and no fiscal-register integration on that page — and Mellon separately maintains a certification matrix covering roughly 70 Greek accounting and retail software products against its terminal interconnection, which is a real integration cost any challenger has to displace (A6). Commercially, Worldline's chief executive said on the H1-2026 call that "Greece is doing extremely well, double-digit on acquiring", with the group's own release naming Greece among its few growth engines; Worldline also completed full ownership of its Greek entity and WON A CONTRACT WITH THE GREEK TAX AUTHORITY to enable clearing of non-domestic card payments through the national clearing platform — extending from merchant acquiring into state payments plumbing at the same authority that sets terminal and fiscal-integration rules (A6). Euronet added 4,200 merchants in the quarter through a Greek acquiring referral programme reaching merchants through third-party channel partners rather than bank branches (A6).

bank_theme: Optima bank — cash-in white space against a capex ceiling
signal: Optima's H1-2026 filings state verbatim that "each branch of the Bank's network has an external automatic teller machine to serve customers who wish to use their debit/credit cards to make cash withdrawals or balance inquiries" — NO DEPOSIT, CASH-IN OR RECYCLING FUNCTION is disclosed anywhere, and the bank's own locator returns 32 sites of which 29 carry an ATM, with no off-site machines at all. Deposits meanwhile grew 37% year on year to €7.1bn and are guided to €8.0bn, on a branch network frozen at 30 sites for four consecutive quarters with a cost-to-core-income ratio of 22.6% (A1). That is the cleanest cash-automation white space of any Greek bank — but it is bounded by a hard constraint: additions to fixed assets were only €737k in H1-2026 (down year on year) plus €1.1m of intangibles, roughly €1.8m of half-year capex in total, which will not absorb a capital purchase of deposit-capable machines. The bank's tariff, reissued 20/07/2026, prices withdrawals at zero at other banks' machines nationwide, so it free-rides the national network and has no commercial reason to expand for withdrawals — any case must be built on cash-IN and teller-replacement economics (A1). Remote identification is already live and load-bearing as a primary account-opening channel, so eKYC is a replacement sale rather than greenfield, and the vendor is disclosed nowhere. There is no merchant acquiring or point-of-sale line at all. The Euroxx Securities acquisition remains guided to complete by end-2026 with no binding agreement on the record, which would pull brokerage onboarding, AML screening and market-surveillance work forward (A1). The master row's two open security vendor selections — data-loss prevention and firewall policy management — were last disclosed as unclosed and are not re-reported this cycle (A1, carried forward).

bank_theme: Greece — cash access policy: merchant cash-out and the EU legal-tender file
signal: Two policy currents that pull Greek cash infrastructure in opposite directions both moved this cycle. FIRST, in a written answer to a parliamentary question tabled 15/06/2026 about the removal of the only ATM in the village of Delvinaki, the Secretary General for the Financial Sector confirmed that under the revised EU payment-services framework Greece negotiated, RETAIL MERCHANTS WILL BE ABLE TO PROVIDE CASH WITHDRAWALS FROM THEIR SHOPS ON A VOLUNTARY BASIS EVEN WITHOUT A PRIOR PURCHASE, aimed at areas with limited ATM or branch access, with merchants earning a small commission; several outlets report a €50 cap per purchase-free withdrawal. The same answer restates that siting branches and ATMs remains a commercial decision of the banks. The MP who raised it argued instead for a legal obligation to keep an ATM in specified peripheral areas (A1, A5). No Greek bill was tabled as at 31/08/2026 (A5). SECOND, and pulling the other way, the European Parliament confirmed by plenary on 08/07/2026 its negotiating mandate on the regulation on the legal tender of euro banknotes and coins: member states would designate authorities overseeing cash acceptance and access and file an annual assessment against common indicators to be set by an implementing act, the named indicators including DENSITY OF CASH ACCESS POINTS RELATIVE TO POPULATION; where an assessment is negative the state must adopt remedies including geographical access requirements, and if it fails to act the Commission may impose country-specific measures. The Council position additionally prohibits refusal of cash except in narrow cases and mandates resilience measures to keep cash payments working during major electronic outages. Whether the density indicator survives into the final text is unverified (A3).

sources.text: Dimokratiki tis Rodou — reporting the Ministry's written answer, 21/08/2026

date: 21/08/2026 — the Ministry's written answer confirming purchase-free merchant cash withdrawals is reported; 08/07/2026 European Parliament plenary confirms the negotiating mandate on the euro legal-tender regulation
implies: Two opposite futures for Greek cash access, and only one of them is a hardware opportunity. Purchase-free cash at retail creates a new product surface — cash-out-enabled terminals, merchant reconciliation and float management, small-safe tooling rather than full cash-in-transit — and simultaneously caps rural ATM demand, which matters most for the banks with the largest rural fleets. A surviving cash-access-density obligation would do the reverse, forcing additional machines in thin areas plus recyclers to make marginal sites economic, monitoring to evidence uptime, and offline-capable dispensing under the resilience clause. Neither is law yet, so a density gap analysis can be sold today only as scenario planning, never as compliance.
likelihood: Medium — the Greek debate is live but no bill is tabled; the EU file plausibly reaches political agreement around end-2026 with the density indicator unconfirmed
follow_up: Retrieve the actual written parliamentary answer from the Hellenic Parliament register to fix the €50 cap and the exact wording before quoting it. Obtain the consolidated parliamentary report on the legal-tender file and confirm whether the density indicator and the Commission backstop survive in the mandate's articles rather than only in a pre-vote summary. Track both branches of the Greek debate — a rural ATM obligation and a merchant cash-out regime lead to completely different propositions.

bank_theme: Hungary — Act XVIII rural ATM rollout + MNB validation/uptime mandate
signal: WHAT MOVED: two agents independently parsed Annex 1 of MNB decree 19/2025 (VI. 26.) line by line and reproduced the same allocation — 80 settlement packages covering 1,039 named settlements, each package assigned to ONE obligated bank: OTP Bank 428 settlements in 33 packages, MBH 195 in 15, K&H 117 in 9, Erste Bank Hungary 104 in 8, Raiffeisen 65 in 5, CIB 52 in 4, UniCredit Hungary 52 in 4, Gránit 13 in 1, MagNet 13 in 1 (A2, A3). Both decrees were re-read from the consolidated texts this cycle and are still in force unamended. The package-swap deadline of 28/02/2026 has passed, so the bank-by-settlement map is now fixed for 2026, and a hand-over of operation cannot be contracted for less than five years — whoever equips a package holds it for years. Every one of the 1,039 machines must be barrier-free under NGM decree 16/2025 §2, and because all enter service after June 2025 none can use the accessibility legacy derogation; MNB Recommendation 6/2025 separately expects each bank to inventory and publish per-machine accessibility attributes down to settlement level, including speech support or push-button entry where a PIN is typed on a touchscreen (A3). The fine ladder is HUF 2m–200m initially, then HUF 5m at three months of continued non-compliance rising step by step to HUF 200m at thirty months. OTP, joined by Erste and Raiffeisen, filed a constitutional complaint on 10/11/2025 and no Constitutional Court decision could be found (A2, A5). NEWLY CLOSED THIS CYCLE: the rollout generates ZERO procurement notices — a full CSV sweep of the Hungarian public-procurement register (EKR) returned no ATM supply procedure of any kind in 2026, because the nine obliged institutions are private banks and are not contracting authorities for this spend (A2).

That means dispense hardware with accessibility packages, remote monitoring and telemetry (there is no branch staff nearby to clear a jam), vendor-neutral ATM software so a bank does not lock 400 rural sites to one manufacturer, physical security for unattended sites, and rural-SLA field service. The five-year minimum on hand-over contracts and the three-yearly re-allocation both argue for a software layer that survives a site changing hands.
