bank_theme: Hungary — Act XIV of 2026 ATM decommissioning and relocation freeze
signal: Act XIV of 2026 §96(1)-(2) rewrote section 3 of the ATM Act with effect from 14/05/2026, and the consolidated statute was re-read verbatim by two agents this cycle (A3, A5). A credit institution may no longer cease operating any ATM that existed when the Act came into force, and the same no-closure rule now covers a branch's cash-payout service — but REPLACEMENT of the machine is expressly carved out ("ide nem értve az ATM cseréjét"). A relocation is permitted only in a justified case and only if an ATM keeps operating in the same settlement or Budapest district; justified cases are listed as moving into a settlement with no ATM at all, evidence from average cash-withdrawal volume data, or the landlord terminating the site lease. Crucially, subsection (1b) anticipates that a like-for-like swap may be impossible at a site "for purely technological or technical reasons — in particular the DIMENSIONS of the new ATM and its SECURITY REQUIREMENTS", in which case the replacement machine may be installed elsewhere in the same settlement. Breach carries an MNB fine of HUF 2m–200m. A1 records the same amendment from OTP's side and notes OTP nonetheless cut its Hungarian estate by 58 machines in H1-2026.

sources.text: Act XVIII of 2025, consolidated text in force from 14/05/2026

date: 14/05/2026 — the decommissioning and relocation freeze enters into force, and every Hungarian ATM refresh decision from that date runs through these rules
implies: Hungary has legislated its ATM estate into a guaranteed replacement market: roughly 5,700 machines nationally can only be swapped, never retired. The statute itself contemplates that the replacement machine may be physically bigger and carry higher security requirements than the one it replaces — which is exactly what happens when a legacy through-the-wall dispenser is swapped for a deeper deposit or recycling machine, or for one carrying accessibility hardware. That converts a shrinking-fleet story into a multi-year refresh pipeline, and adds two attached sales: a chargeable site-survey and fit study for machines that will not fit their old holes, and withdrawal-volume telemetry, because a bank now needs volume evidence to justify any move.
likelihood: High — the law is in force and binds every refresh decision already being taken
follow_up: Take the replacement pipeline separately from the 1,039 rural sites to each of the nine banks — lead with recycler-class upgrades plus a paid site-survey and fit study against subsection (1b), and attach withdrawal-volume telemetry as the evidence a bank needs to justify a relocation. Obtain Act XIV §96 from the Magyar Közlöny and its explanatory memorandum; ask MNB whether a replacement that fails the (1b) test needs prior notification.

bank_theme: OTP Bank Hungary and Erste Bank Hungary — cash-in white space against a shrinking OTP estate
signal: OTP's H1-2026 statutory report of 05/08/2026 puts OTP Core Hungary at 299 branches, 1,929 ATMs and 149,868 POS terminals at 30/06/2026, down from 301, 1,987 and 150,158 at 31/12/2025 — a net loss of 58 ATMs, or 2.9%, in six months, and 69 fewer than at 31/03/2026 (A1). bank_theme: Hungary — 2026-27 payments-infrastructure deadline stack: the VIBER address gap and the instant-euro build
signal: Two dated obligations land on the same nine Hungarian banks inside fifteen months, and one of them has a verified Hungarian-specific hole in it. FIRST, the address break. The European Payments Council's guidance EPC153-22 v2.1 fixes 15/11/2026 as the date from which an unstructured postal address is no longer permitted in the SEPA scheme rulebooks and "will hence lead to rejects", on both the inter-bank leg and corporate file upload; the same weekend carries the SWIFT standards release, and Germany's Bundesbank independently confirms the removal of unstructured postal address data from the European RTGS system's messages with production deployment on 14/11/2026 and the real hard stop — the end of release testing — on 28/10/2026. AGAINST THAT, A3 downloaded and text-extracted the MNB's currently effective business terms and their annexes and found ZERO occurrences of "ISO 20022", "strukturált cím" or "hibrid" anywhere in the effective annex set, including annexes updated as recently as 03/08/2026: Hungary's domestic real-time gross settlement system VIBER runs ISO 20022 messages but has NO structured or hybrid postal-address rule and no date, eleven weeks before the international cutover. SECOND, the instant-euro calendar for non-euro EU states, re-read from the Regulation itself and corrected this cycle: 09/01/2027 Hungarian banks must be able to RECEIVE instant euro credit transfers and must price instant transfers no higher than equivalent non-instant ones with payee-verification services free of charge; 09/04/2027 the same receiving duty reaches electronic-money and payment institutions; 09/07/2027 all non-euro payment service providers must SEND instant euro AND provide Verification of Payee, the payee-name-to-account match. Two reliefs exist — a carve-out until 09/06/2028 for national-currency accounts, and a right to ask the MNB for permission to cap outside-business-hours sending (A3).

implies: Hungarian banks will run TWO address regimes concurrently across the same customer base — structured or hybrid for SEPA and correspondent traffic from mid-November, free-text still permitted domestically — and that dual-regime problem is the sale: dual-format handling, reject and rejection-message monitoring at cutover, sanctions and anti-money-laundering screening re-tuned onto the structured town and country fields, and customer-data cleansing that satisfies the international leg without breaking the domestic one. bank_theme: Kosovo — POS whitespace + deposit-ATM upgrade (BPB Printec-incumbent)
signal: The market numbers moved hard this cycle. The central bank's August-2026 card report (data to 31/12/2025) shows card-accepting POS terminals reaching about 30,300, up from 20,913 a year earlier — a 45% jump of roughly 9,400 terminals deployed in a single twelve-month period, and the largest single movement in Kosovo's payment infrastructure (A1, A4). The ATM picture went the other way: the fleet grew only 8% to 686 machines, of which just 394 can accept a cash deposit and only 57 can originate a credit transfer. Because banks added dispensers faster than deposit-capable machines, the deposit-capable share actually FELL from 59.4% to 57.4%, so the cash-in gap WIDENED to 292 machines that cannot take a deposit and 629 that cannot make a transfer (A1). The commercial case is now quantified: ATM deposits carry 32.1% of all card-transaction value on those 394 machines, while POS payments carry only 17.8% — the highest-value work in the country is done by the smallest and least-equipped part of the estate. Monthly data to June 2026 show both flows still accelerating: ATM deposit counts +14.0% year-on-year, ATM withdrawals +10.5%, POS payments +47.0% (A4). Terminals offering cash-back at the till rose from 18 to 245 in one year, an early sign of merchant-based cash-out substituting for ATMs.

bank_theme: Kosovo — KIPS upgrade and instant-payment bank-side integration across all banks
signal: The programme moved from planning into live operation this cycle. Banca d'Italia confirmed that the shared TIPS Clone instant-payment platform — a standalone copy of the European Central Bank's TARGET Instant Payment Settlement system, built for the Western Balkans — officially WENT LIVE on 20/07/2026, with the central banks of Bosnia and Herzegovina and Montenegro as the first joiners, and that a second onboarding window is scheduled for November 2026 when the central banks of Albania, Kosovo and North Macedonia are expected to join (A3, A4). The platform settles in participating countries' own currencies in central bank money and in euro in commercial bank money — a dual-money model with separate screening and reconciliation consequences. Kosovo's central bank has now bought both of the pieces it needed: the connectivity layer, awarded to Nexi (see the separate Nexi row), and a ten-month advisory contract for design and programme management, awarded to Paylume SRL of Brussels at EUR 295,000 on 22/07/2026 from exactly one expression of interest (A2). The central bank's Annual Report 2025 names the four overlay schemes being scoped on top of the national system — QR Code, Request to Pay, Proxy ID and Verification of Payee — and records that during 2025 it signed an agreement with the European Payments Council for use of the SCT, SDD and SCT Inst schemes (A4). At sector level, the Banking Association's payments committee chair has stated commercial banks' full commitment to join, and the central bank's own invited expert framed the work as "elimination of existing technical gaps" (A3, A5) — but no commercial-bank connection date has been published anywhere.

bank_theme: Banka Qendrore e Kosovës (BQK) — centralised IT access-management project, twice unfilled
signal: The central bank's open supply procedure for the supply and implementation of a centralised access-management project for its IT systems — in effect a privileged access management platform, the software that controls and records who can use administrator-level accounts — procurement number BQK 26 061 111, was CANCELLED on 24/08/2026. date: 24/08/2026 — procedure cancelled after both bids failed responsiveness; re-tender expected

bank_theme: Kosovo — CBK Regulation on Information Systems and Cyber Risk Management (Kosovo's DORA)
signal: Kosovo's equivalent of the EU's digital operational resilience rules is now BINDING and its compliance date has already passed. The central bank's board approved the regulation on 29/08/2025; it entered into force on 15/09/2025 and Article 67 obliged financial institutions to comply FROM 01/06/2026. It is a roughly 50-page rulebook covering governance, ICT asset and information management, management of third-party service providers, budget forecasting, project management and IT acquisition, secure development, testing, patch deployment, access rights and cloud services (A3, A4). It EXCEEDS the EU minimum on incident timing: Article 31(10) requires notification to the central bank no later than FOUR HOURS after discovery, an interim report within 72 hours and a final report within 30 days, and the reporting template demands the hardware manufacturer, software developer and make and model of the affected applications and the systems they run on. The template explicitly names ATMs — "bankomatet" — alongside SWIFT, RTGS and ACH as critical systems whose compromise must be declared (A4). Commercially the sharpest clause is Article 10: institutions must allocate sufficient budget for cyber preparedness AND "the cybersecurity budget should be independent of the FI's overall ICT budget, to ensure that business-related systems developments do not compete for resources allocated to protecting ICT systems" (A3).

sources.text: CBK — Regulation on Information Systems and Cyber Risk Management (English, PDF)

date: 01/06/2026 — the compliance obligation took effect for every Kosovo financial institution; supervisory examination, not preparation, is now the live conversation
implies: Every Kosovo bank is non-compliant today if it cannot produce an ICT asset register, a third-party provider register, a documented patch process and a four-hour incident pipeline. Because the reporting template names ATMs as regulated critical infrastructure and demands make, model and firmware evidence, this converts directly into ATM and device telemetry and monitoring, multi-vendor estate visibility software, managed field services for documented patching, auditable encryption key management and remote key injection, and real-time transaction monitoring. The ring-fenced cybersecurity budget in Article 10 is the single most useful clause in the market: it forces a board-visible spending line that ordinary business projects are forbidden to cannibalise. Kosovo has no firm SEPA date, so this — not payments — is the near-term spend trigger.
likelihood: High — binding since 01/06/2026 and supervisory enforcement is the next step
follow_up: Offer every Kosovo bank a gap assessment against this regulation, built on device telemetry and an ICT asset register that produces the four-hour incident evidence, and lead the commercial conversation with the Article 10 ring-fenced budget. Ask the central bank's supervision department whether on-site inspections have begun and how it intends to examine ATM-estate compliance.

bank_theme: TEB Sh.A. (BNP Paribas / TEB group), Kosovo — recurring cash-handling, digital-onboarding and ATM-services tender cycle
signal: TEB runs a large public tender board carrying roughly 100 invitation-for-bid notices with downloadable documents, several squarely in Printec's scope, and it is the only Kosovo commercial bank that publishes its buying at this scale (A1, A2). Confirmed from the documents themselves: Tender 259/26 "Supply of Cash Handling Machines" — counting and sorting for coins and banknotes — issued 22/05/2026 and closed 02/06/2026, a REPEAT of Tender 292/25 of June 2025, so an annual cycle with a predictable next window around May-June 2027; Tender 270/26 "Remote (Digital) Onboarding & Digital Signature Integration", issued 28/05/2026 and extended TWICE to a final close of 29/06/2026, which plainly shows it struggled to attract qualified bidders; Tender 311/26 "E Archive Project", issued 22/06/2026 and closed 03/07/2026, itself a SECOND attempt after an identical project ran in April 2025; Tender 031/26 thermal paper rolls for POS terminals; Tender 636/24 covering physical security, cash-in-transit, ATM REPLENISHMENT and monitoring-room supervision, confirming TEB outsources its ATM estate; and Ref 375-25 for ATM kiosk production and servicing. TEB publishes invitations, re-tenders and deadline extensions but NEVER award notices, and no budget figure appears in any notice — all dossiers are released only on request to procurement@teb-kos.com. Nothing has been published since June 2026. Behind this sits a counted estate: 83 to 87 ATMs against 35 branches on the bank's own locator as at 27/08/2026, with cardless QR-code cash withdrawal newly marketed as "the newest ATM service for our customers", and no mention of deposit or 24/7 capability anywhere on the estate pages (A1). On the intent side, four roles were advertised simultaneously for the Deçan location with a 25/08/2026 deadline, and the bank's Qafa branch in Prishtina is relocating (A5).
date: 25/08/2026 — a four-role staffing cluster for the Deçan location closed and the Qafa Prishtina branch relocation is live; the 2026 cash-handling lot closed 02/06/2026 and the annual cycle reopens around May-June 2027
implies: The most concrete, repeatable way into a Kosovo commercial bank. TEB buys banknote and coin counting and sorting machines annually, buys ATM and POS thermal paper as a recurring consumable, tenders ATM kiosk production and servicing, outsources cash-in-transit plus ATM replenishment and monitoring, and is actively trying to buy a remote-onboarding and qualified electronic-signature stack that it has failed twice to land. The cardless QR withdrawal launch means TEB has recently touched its ATM application software — the moment a bank is most open to a wider self-service conversation — while the total absence of deposit language across an 85-machine estate makes it a prime candidate for a dispenser-heavy fleet needing recycler upgrade. A branch relocation and a four-role staffing cluster both put fit-out budget in play. All Unscoped because TEB publishes no budgets and no winners.

follow_up: Email procurement@teb-kos.com to get onto the standing bidder list, and ask who was awarded 259/26, 270/26 and 311/26, whether 270/26 was awarded at all given two extensions, and whether it requires a Kosovo-accredited qualified trust service provider. Diarise May 2027 for the next cash-handling lot. Ask how many of the ~85 machines are deposit-capable, who supplied the cardless QR application, and — since TEB is a BNP Paribas and Türk Ekonomi Bankası joint venture — whether ATM decisions are taken in Istanbul rather than Prishtina.

bank_theme: ProCredit Bank Kosova — 29-site branch-light estate and an open numbered tender programme
signal: ProCredit Kosovo runs a markedly branch-light network: its own locator, re-counted 27/08/2026, shows 29 physical sites made up of 15 branches with an ATM on site, 13 stand-alone ATMs and one formal "ATM Zone" at Prishtina Mall. The stand-alone machines are deliberately off-premise — petrol stations, malls, a military base — exactly the estate that needs remote monitoring, cash forecasting and managed first-line service. The bank markets the fleet as round-the-clock and deposit-capable but does not publish how many machines actually accept deposits, and it sells a named service for cash deposits above EUR 10,000 (A1). Alongside this it runs an open, numbered, roughly monthly tender programme routed to a single group procurement mailbox: reference numbering had reached T-0010 by August 2026, and the posted lots include supply of coins and banknote bags (closed 09/06/2026), supply of UPS units and UPS batteries (offers due 25/08/2026), fuel and charging for the electric vehicle fleet, motorcycles and bancassurance. Financially the unit has headroom: total assets EUR 1,503m and profit after tax EUR 13.1m at 30/06/2026 — the group's second-largest single-bank profit — with a capital adequacy ratio of 15.9% and a NEW EUR 16.0m "other capital instruments" line appearing in the quarter, nil the quarter before. Group practice on identity is informative: the banking app is built in-house by the group's own IT subsidiary Quipu, but electronic identity and signature are BOUGHT from local qualified providers per market, which makes the Kosovo identity slot a genuine vendor-selected procurement (A1). ProCredit also fielded an acceptance lead at the national Tap-to-Phone merchant roadshow (A4, A5).

implies: A 29-site estate is small enough to be replaced in one or two awards rather than piecemeal, which makes it a realistic single-award target for self-service hardware plus managed services. What the bank actually buys is telling: uninterruptible power supplies and batteries for a machine estate, and coin and banknote bags — precisely the adjacencies a managed-services provider absorbs into a single availability contract covering power, consumables and first-line maintenance. bank_theme: Kosovo — softPOS / Tap-to-Phone shift in merchant acceptance
signal: A national Tap-to-Phone programme — "Paguaj me një TAP" — is steering Kosovo merchant acceptance onto ordinary Android phones rather than dedicated card terminals. It is run by the Kosovo Banking Association with Visa, Helvetas, Sweden/Sverige and the IMAA, opened by the association's chief executive with the central bank's Payments Department director presenting the regulator's next steps. Two merchant events are firmly evidenced, in Prishtina on 16/04/2026 and Prizren on 25/05/2026, with THREE banks fielding live propositions: Raiffeisen Bank Kosovo, NLB Banka and ProCredit Bank Kosovo (A4, A5). The underlying acceptance demand is real and measured: about 9,400 net-new POS terminals in 2025 and POS payment counts up 47% year-on-year in June 2026 (A1, A4). CAVEAT: the two agents disagree on whether the roadshow continued past May — A4 records "Paguaj me një TAP" entries for Gjakovë dated June 2026 on the association's events calendar while also stating two other claimed dates do not exist, and A5 records that the association has published nothing since 25/05/2026. Phone-based acceptance compresses demand for classic POS hardware in the micro-merchant segment where most of Kosovo's growth is happening — a genuine threat to a terminal-led position. But it does not remove the back end: softPOS still needs merchant onboarding and electronic identity checks, device and terminal management, encryption key injection and hardware-security-module-backed protection behind a phone-based PIN, plus certified attestation for the acquirer. The message is to sell the platform, not the box. The four banks WITHOUT a live Tap-to-Phone product — TEB, BKT, Banka Ekonomike and Banka për Biznes — are the addressable white space; the three that are live are warm entry points on the back end.

bank_theme: Kosovo — remote onboarding and electronic identity: national eID, the ARC remote data-update regulation, and unmet bank demand
signal: Three strands converged this cycle. First, the state layer: the European Commission's Kosovo Report 2025 confirms Kosovo adopted a Law on electronic identification and trust services, that a national electronic identity system became operational in 2024, that the national eID and eWallet are in a launched piloting phase, and that 230 online services now run on the e-Kosova portal — but the law tracks the first-generation EU eIDAS framework, not the new Digital Identity Framework, so a further alignment amendment is expected and no production date for the eWallet is published (A3). Second, a concrete legal unlock: the Civil Registration Agency, supported by the Banking Association, FINALISED a draft Ministry of Internal Affairs regulation allowing bank customers' personal data to be updated REMOTELY without physical presence in a branch, for customers assessed as low risk. The draft was agreed by all relevant parties on 12/05/2026 but its adoption and publication remain unconfirmed three months later (A5). Third, demonstrated unmet demand: TEB tendered "Remote (Digital) Onboarding & Digital Signature Integration" (270/26) and had to extend the deadline TWICE to 29/06/2026, which shows the requirement is funded and still unsatisfied (A2). Group practice elsewhere confirms the shape of the buy — ProCredit builds its banking app in-house through Quipu but BUYS electronic identity and signature from local qualified providers market by market, so the Kosovo slot is a genuine vendor selection (A1).
date: 29/06/2026 — TEB's remote-onboarding and digital-signature tender closed after two extensions, with no award published; the Civil Registration Agency remote data-update regulation was agreed 12/05/2026 and awaits adoption
implies: Kosovo is the most advanced non-EU market in the footprint on state electronic identity after Ukraine — a law in force, a national eID operational and an eWallet in pilot — which makes it the best non-EU candidate for a remote-onboarding play bound to the national eID. The Civil Registration Agency regulation is narrower than full remote onboarding: it covers periodic KYC REFRESH for low-risk customers, which still requires an integration to the state civil register plus risk-tiering and screening behind it, so size it as a data-refresh integration rather than a greenfield onboarding platform. TEB's twice-extended tender is the proof that at least one bank is trying to buy this now and cannot find a qualified bidder.
likelihood: Medium — the pilot is running and the draft regulation is agreed, but neither has a published production or compliance date; the near-term pull is bank demand rather than a deadline
follow_up: Confirm whether the Civil Registration Agency regulation has been ADOPTED and published in the Official Gazette since May 2026 and get its compliance date — that date is the sales trigger; check the Ministry of Internal Affairs and the Gazette directly rather than waiting on the association. Ask the central bank whether the national eID is accepted as a standalone customer-due-diligence identification method for remote account opening. Approach TEB about 270/26 and the other six banks with the same offer.

bank_theme: Kosovo — Law 08/L-304 on Banks compliance deadline, with the Payment Services law still blocking SEPA
signal: Law No. 08/L-304 on Banks, adopted 05/12/2024, WAS promulgated by presidential decree of 20/01/2026 and published in Official Gazette No. 2 of 27/01/2026, entering into force about 11/02/2026. Article 147(1) gives banks and branches of foreign banks holding a licence at entry into force TWELVE MONTHS to bring themselves into compliance — a statutory date of about 11/02/2027 — with three years for foreign bank branches on certain provisions. Article 1(2) states the law is harmonised with the EU capital requirements regulation and directive and the bank recovery and resolution directive. That leaves only the Payment Services law 08/L-328 and the AML/CFT law 08/L-333 caught in constitutional review. The central bank says the consequence in its own annual report, verbatim: the restrictions arising from non-promulgation "prevented the final application to SEPA and, consequently, resulted in the loss of the opportunity to keep pace with neighbouring countries". A replacement route is already moving — the Government approved a new Draft Law on Payment Services at its 8th meeting by Decision No. 08/08 of 03/04/2026, heading to the Assembly. The same blockage gates a second opportunity: the central bank's Regulation on access of non-bank payment service providers to payment systems, adopted 25/11/2025, lets non-bank providers open settlement accounts directly in the national system, but its Article 18 states it enters into force ten days after Law 08/L-328 does (A4).

sources.text: Official Gazette of the Republic of Kosovo No. 2 / 27 January 2026, Law No. 08/L-304 on Banks

date: 11/02/2027 — the statutory deadline for every licensed Kosovo bank to be in compliance with Law 08/L-304 on Banks; the Payment Services law 08/L-328 remains unpromulgated and a replacement draft was approved by Government on 03/04/2026
implies: A statutory compliance date roughly five months out on an EU-aligned prudential and resolution law forces regulatory reporting, data-quality and risk-system remediation across every Kosovo bank on a fixed clock — core and channel integration, regulatory reporting and data quality, AML and know-your-customer screening, and managed services. It also removes one of the three blockers to Kosovo's SEPA application, shortening the runway once the remaining two clear. Kosovo is the one Western Balkan market where the SEPA compliance wave is dammed rather than spent: two independent release valves now exist — a court ruling or Assembly passage of the replacement draft — and either would trigger a compressed multi-bank remediation programme. Behind that sits a greenfield buyer class of e-money institutions, payment institutions and fintechs that will join the national system directly and own none of the required infrastructure.
likelihood: High for the 11/02/2027 bank-law deadline, which is statutory and already running; Low for the payment-services unlock within 6-12 months, since commencement depends on a law in constitutional limbo
follow_up: Time bank outreach against the roughly 11/02/2027 adaptation deadline. Track the Assembly agenda for the 03/04/2026 Draft Law on Payment Services — the faster of the two paths — alongside the Constitutional Court docket for a judgment on 08/L-328 and 08/L-333, and check whether the replacement draft renumbers the legal basis the non-bank access regulation relies on, which would force it to be re-issued.

bank_theme: Kosovo — cash-operations compliance spine: the ECB tested-machine gate and the new Counterfeit Monitoring System
signal: Kosovo's Regulation on Cash Operations, board-approved 27/12/2023 and in force since 01/02/2024, was obtained and read in full this cycle and is stronger than previously understood. Article 5(4) provides that processing machines used by financial institutions to check the authenticity and fitness of euro banknotes and coins may only be put into use if they have been SUCCESSFULLY TESTED BY THE EUROSYSTEM; Article 5(5) requires banknote machines in use or planned to appear on the European Central Bank's published list of tested machines and coin machines on the European Commission's equivalent list; and Articles 17(3) and 18(3) extend the same requirement explicitly to machines operated by the customer. Article 22 transposes the ECB machine taxonomy in full — cash-in, cash-recycling, combined cash-in and cash-out — with recyclers required to check both authenticity and fitness. The regulation also bars any person from providing cash deposit or withdrawal services through customer-operated machines, or importing or holding such machines, without a central-bank licence. A linked implementation plan of 12/02/2024 commits the central bank to "the deployment of several ATMs and other devices enabling the electronic payments (POS), or financial self-services" in Serb-majority municipalities including the four northern ones (A1). New this cycle: on 15/07/2026 the central bank announced it had begun EU-supported activities to establish a Kosovo Counterfeit Monitoring System — though only the headline and date are verified, because the site sits behind a Cloudflare gate and no archive copy exists (A1). The volume behind all this: about 20.65 million euro banknotes, 33.23% of everything banks deposited in 2025, were classified unfit and withdrawn, against total banknote operations of EUR 6.73bn and 132.5 million pieces (A4).

bank_theme: Montenegro — instant payments live at all 11 banks: Verification of Payee mandate, irrevocable rail, 5-cent fee cap
signal: On 20/07/2026 the Central Bank of Montenegro put the TIPS Clone instant-payment platform into production — a national settlement system cloned from the European Central Bank's TARGET Instant Payment Settlement service, built with Banca d'Italia and financed by an EUR 8m World Bank credit. Banca d'Italia confirms Montenegro and Bosnia were the first two central banks to join, with Albania, Kosovo and North Macedonia expected in a second window in November 2026 (A3). Uniquely in the region, the whole sector went live at once: the regulator publishes customer video guides from all eleven banks — Addiko, Adriatic, CKB, Erste, Hipotekarna, Lovćen, NLB, Prva banka, Universal Capital, Zapad banka and Ziraat — and states plainly that all 11 banks are IPS participants (A1, A4). Three things follow for the banks. First, the enabling amendments to the Law on Payment Transactions make Verification of Payee compulsory in line with EU Regulation 2024/886 — before confirming an order the bank must check that the payee name matches the IBAN, warn the customer on a mismatch and do it free of charge, with fines of EUR 10,000-40,000 for non-compliance; funds must reach the payee within ten seconds or be returned without delay (A6). Second, the rail is irrevocable — the regulator's own FAQ says instant payments as a rule cannot be recalled — and two days after go-live the central bank had to warn the public about a phishing wave impersonating itself and Western Union with a fake EUR 50 giveaway link, which is the classic set-up for authorised-push-payment fraud where the victim is tricked into sending the money themselves (A4). Third, a Council Decision of 17/07/2026 caps the fee on a domestic instant transfer up to EUR 200 made by mobile or internet banking at five euro-cents on both the sending and the receiving side, against a previous average of 32 cents, with the regulator estimating EUR 1m of annual savings rising to EUR 2.8m (A1, A4). First official volumes: 56,678 instant transfers worth EUR 21.53m in the 12 days of July, average ticket EUR 380, full availability; the regulator's directorate head reports volume rose five-fold from launch day to end-July and that only "a little over 60%" of credit transfers are currently initiated electronically (A4, A5).
date: 20/07/2026 — TIPS Clone go-live across all 11 banks · 17/07/2026 Council Decision capping the fee at 5 cents · 22/07/2026 central-bank phishing warning · 13/08/2026 first official IPS volumes published · monthly statistics continue, August figures due mid-September 2026
implies: Every Montenegrin bank now carries the same three obligations at the same moment: run real-time payee-name matching, screen for fraud and sanctions inline because a ten-second irrevocable payment makes after-the-fact review useless, and keep a 24/7/365 rail available with no overnight maintenance window. In a market this small that is one packaged offer sold eleven times — real-time transaction monitoring, fraud scoring, a Verification-of-Payee matching engine, and 24/7 managed operations for the banks with thin in-house teams (Adriatic, Zapad, Universal Capital, Ziraat, Lovćen). The 5-cent price ceiling is the commercial lever underneath everything else: it destroys fee income on small payments, so the only way a bank protects margin is by cutting cost-to-serve, which is exactly the self-service and automation case.
likelihood: High — the rail is live, the legal obligations are in force and the bank-side build has to happen over the next 6-12 months
follow_up: Ask each of the 11 banks which engine screens IPS traffic in real time and who supplied their Verification-of-Payee name-matching — the first vendor in becomes the regional incumbent for Albania and Kosovo in November. Offer an authorised-push-payment fraud assessment framed on the central bank's own 22/07/2026 warning. Obtain the text of the payments-law amendments to confirm the VoP wording, which currently rests on press reporting.

bank_theme: Montenegro — instant-payments phase 2 (QR acceptance, phone-number alias, Request-to-Pay) and the digital-channel gap
signal: The regulator has put a date on the next wave. Its own Terms of Reference for the TIPS Clone programme commit to Phase III adoption over Q4-2026 to Q1-2027 and Phase IV overlay services from March 2027 to March 2028, explicitly naming QR-code payments for merchant acceptance and Request-to-Pay; the regulator's public roadmap adds payment by mobile phone number (an alias directory, so customers pay a phone number instead of an IBAN) and preparation for cross-border SEPA Instant (A2, A4). Two facts make this urgent rather than theoretical. A licensed non-bank is already shipping the whole phase-2 experience: PrestoPay DOO Podgorica, register number 07 in the central bank's Register of Payment Institutions, authorised since 14/10/2024 for payment initiation and account information services — a PSD2-style third party that can start payments from and read balances on other banks' accounts — markets alias-based person-to-person payments, split-the-bill requests and camera-and-QR bill scanning, and on 31/08/2026 its app sat at number 45 in Montenegro's overall free-app chart, ahead of every bank app in the country (A4). Meanwhile the banks' own channels are weak: app-store metadata pulled on 31/08/2026 shows almost the entire sector shipped releases in the six weeks around go-live, but four domestic incumbents rate below 2.5 out of 5 — Hipotekarna 2.33, Prva banka 2.26, Lovćen 2.26, Erste Montenegro 2.37, NLB 2.77 — while the only strong local performer is Addiko at 4.69 on 514 ratings, roughly ten times any other bank's review base (A4). Underlying demand is there: 304,691 mobile-payment users at Q1-2026, about 48% of the population, growing every quarter with no seasonal dip, against 498,969 card users; internet-payment users 321,203, though the legal-entity component is falling (70,313 → 57,471) as businesses consolidate onto mobile and office banking (A4).

Terminals reached 23,250 at Q1-2026 from 18,775 at Q4-2024 — a net +4,475 in five quarters and an all-time high — and unlike the ATM fleet, POS does not dip seasonally and has risen every quarter since Q1-2024; e-money-accepting terminals rose to 4,632 and cards with a payment function to 573,740 (A4). bank_theme: Montenegro — branch and counter cash automation (teller recyclers, business cash deposit)
signal: Cash at the counter is falling steadily but is still enormous, and it is overwhelmingly a business flow. Over-the-counter cash orders fell from 6.81m in 2022 to 5.48m in 2025 (-19.5%) and 1,197,753 in Q1-2026 (-6.0% year on year), but the value is still EUR 5.77bn a year, and within 2025 cash deposits by companies and entrepreneurs were EUR 2.95bn of the EUR 3.62bn total deposit value — 81% — while 88% of withdrawal value went to individuals (A4). Against that, ATM cash deposits in Q1-2026 were only EUR 42.7m, about 6% of the counter deposit value (A1). Banks are already acting on it. CKB reopened its Podgorica Business Point on 24/07/2026 as a small-business centre where cash transactions are no longer available at the counter at all, with non-cash transfers running only through a six-month transition that closes around 24/01/2027, directing customers to ATMs for withdrawal and to cash-in devices for free deposit of daily takings; it had already run a two-month campaign paying EUR 20 each to the first 500 customers who deposited at an ATM twice and never used a teller (A1). Two banks still run manual overnight cash drops that a smart safe or deposit recycler replaces outright — NLB publishes 11 day-and-night safes as a separate location type and Erste 12 across 10 addresses (A1). The market's reference build already exists: Addiko Montenegro runs 12 deposit-and-withdrawal machines, seven of them branded self-service "Zona 24/7" lobbies, and uniquely in the region they accept coins as well as notes through a dedicated perforated coin tray, with a 150-banknote limit and a business daily-takings flow tagged by date and organisational unit (A1). Macro backdrop: retail deposits grew 13.45% year on year to June 2026, more than double total deposit growth, on a tourism season up about 6% (A1).

bank_theme: CKB (OTP Group) — counter cash-out at the branch and a managed migration to deposit ATMs
signal: The country's largest bank by branch presence is actively removing cash from its counters. On 24/07/2026 CKB reopened its Podgorica Business Point at Moskovska 2D as a specialised micro and small-business centre where, verbatim, cash transactions are no longer available at the counters, with non-cash transfers continuing only through a six-month transition period; customers are directed to ATMs to withdraw and to cash-in devices to deposit daily takings free of charge, with a free cash-in card issued in branch. Separately the bank ran a two-month campaign from 23 May to 23 July paying EUR 20 to each of the first 500 customers who made at least two ATM cash deposits on different days and made no counter deposit at all — it is paying customers to stop using the teller. The capacity behind that push is thin: CKB's own published maps show roughly 115-117 ATM locations but only 30 cash-in sites, about 26% of the fleet, with 13 of the 30 in Podgorica, so about 87 machines are withdrawal-only (A1). Its parent's half-year report confirms the direction at group level — CKB's branches fell from 26 to 24 in the first half of 2026 while ATMs held flat at 106 and terminals grew from 11,603 to 12,116 (A1).

bank_theme: Montenegro — CRD VI / CRR III and resolution alignment, with EU accession negotiations targeted to close by end-2026
signal: On 03/07/2026 the central bank's Council approved a draft Law amending the Law on Credit Institutions, aligning Montenegro primarily with the final European CRD VI and CRR III prudential packages and with the regulations underpinning the Single Supervisory Mechanism and the European Central Bank close-cooperation regime, explicitly framed around the central bank's future integration into the European System of Central Banks. The Council also approved a draft Law amending the Law on Resolution of Credit Institutions, aligning with the Single Resolution Mechanism and Single Resolution Fund with deferred application of the post-accession provisions, and held the countercyclical capital buffer at 1%. Montenegro's stated strategic goal is to conclude EU accession negotiations by end-2026; the central bank coordinates Chapter 9 on financial services and Chapter 17 on economic and monetary policy, and on 24/08/2026 welcomed constitutional amendments strengthening its independence (A4). There is an explicit contradiction in the raw evidence about digital operational resilience: an earlier press report of a September 2025 Council draft claimed the amendments would carry the EU DORA operational-resilience requirements, but that press source could not be re-read this cycle and the central bank's own pages returned errors, while the agent reading the 03/07/2026 approval states the draft contains no DORA transposition article (A3, A4).
date: 03/07/2026 — Council approves the CRD VI/CRR III and resolution draft laws · end-2026 stated target for concluding EU accession negotiations · parliamentary adoption expected within that timetable
implies: Importing the EU prudential package pulls in the whole compliance stack that sits behind it — anti-money-laundering and sanctions screening, regulatory reporting and data quality, hardware security modules and PIN key management, and information and communications technology resilience work. An end-2026 negotiation-closing target compresses the timeline into the next 12-18 months, which is unusually tight for a legislative programme of this size. The digital-operational-resilience element must NOT be presented to a customer as fact until the draft text is read: the two agents disagree about whether it is in the bill at all.
likelihood: Medium-High — both drafts approved by the Council, parliamentary adoption expected inside the accession timetable
follow_up: Obtain the draft Law on Credit Institutions text and settle whether an operational-resilience article is in it — until then do not carry a Montenegrin DORA obligation into any forecast. Track when the amendments reach the Skupština and position screening, reporting and key-management accordingly.

bank_theme: North Macedonia — instant payments arrive on two rails (TIPS Clone + KIBS Instant), MIPS rebuilt on ISO 20022
signal: North Macedonia is about to get real-time payments on two separate systems at once, and every bank has to connect to both. Banca d'Italia's TIPS Clone — a copy of the euro-area instant settlement service, built for the Western Balkans — went live on 20/07/2026 with Bosnia and Montenegro, and a second joining window in November 2026 is expected to bring North Macedonia in alongside Albania and Kosovo (A3, A5). ECB President Lagarde referred to the accession on 24/07/2026 and the National Bank (NBRSM) repeated it, but both say "expected", with no day named (A4). In parallel NBRSM confirmed on 04/08/2026 that during July it completed the FIRST TESTING CYCLE of the rebuilt MIPS national payment system with the banks, with most project messages processed in ISO 20022 — the international payment-message standard (A4). Separately KIBS, the private clearing house, already holds an instant-payment operator licence for denar payments settled in under 10 seconds 24/7 and runs the "Strela" app with QR, contactless, an alias register and request-to-pay; trade press reports two banks preparing to initiate over it by 15/09/2026, names not published (A1, A5). NBRSM's own statistics still report ZERO instant payments in every month from Jan-2024 to Mar-2026, so this is a standing start with a clean "before" baseline (A4). NBRSM and the World Bank ran a two-day readiness workshop for banks and PSPs on 16/06/2026 focused explicitly on participants' technical and operational readiness (A3).
date: 04/08/2026 — first MIPS test cycle completed on ISO 20022; 15/09/2026 — first banks expected to initiate on KIBS Instant; November 2026 — expected TIPS Clone joining window
implies: Every one of the seven main NBRSM-licensed banks faces two integrations, not one, on two different calendars. Each needs ISO 20022 message mapping, 24/7/365 channel and liquidity operations, real-time sanctions and fraud screening that clears in seconds (an overnight batch cannot score a payment that settles instantly), key management and HSMs for the new scheme, and QR acceptance across the terminal estate. This is the single largest discrete opportunity in the market and the same work repeats across the whole TIPS Clone bloc.
likelihood: High that the MIPS ISO 20022 go-live proceeds — first test cycle passed and the project is EU-funded; Medium-High specifically on the November-2026 instant window, which NBRSM and the ECB both call "expected" rather than fixed
follow_up: Ask NBRSM's Payment Systems Department (director Biljana Donovska-Gecheva) for the exact go-live date and the wave-one bank list, and request the TIPS Clone message specification — the assumption that it carries ISO 20022 pacs messages is currently unsourced and must not be repeated to a client as fact. Identify the two banks joining KIBS Instant by 15/09/2026. Re-pull NBRSM Table 7 after November to catch the first non-zero instant month.

bank_theme: North Macedonia — central bank's merchant-acceptance programme: national QR, aliases, request-to-pay and low-cost softPOS
signal: The central bank has publicly made small-merchant card acceptance its priority and named cheap acceptance devices as the answer. At the NBRSM–World Bank stakeholder forum on 18/06/2026, Vice-Governor Igor Velichkovski said 84% of citizens hold a payment account and three in four have paid digitally, yet more than 90% of payments at SMALL merchants are still cash, and only about 16,700 merchants hold roughly 36,000 accepting devices — a base he called concentrated and unequal. His named remedies are instant payments "by the end of the year", a NATIONAL INTEROPERABLE QR code usable across all providers, payments by simple alias, instant confirmation of every transaction, request-to-pay, and more mobile apps including from non-bank providers; he named the high cost of acceptance devices as a core barrier (A4). The banks are already moving: NLB launched "NLB Smart POS", the first certified tap-on-phone Android application in the country (a merchant's own phone becomes the terminal, no hardware), with installations up 46% year on year and transaction volume doubled, and is giving 50 free softPOS units under the "Value of Cashless Payment — Bitola" project that closed enrolment on 31/08/2026; Halkbank is running a parallel "Cashless Bitola" offer on its Halk Mobi POS (A5). NLB Group has separately quantified a regional acquiring push with end-to-end POS-to-cash-register integration and softPOS on the 2026-2030 roadmap (A1). KIBS's own cost-benefit work for the World Bank counted converting part of the grey economy into formal payment channels as a benefit of instant payments (A1). NBRSM's Q1-2026 data shows payments at physical points of sale still grew 11.7% year on year even as mobile took 72.8% of electronically initiated payments — the terminal estate is being extended, not cannibalised (A4).

That is an explicit opening for tap-to-phone softPOS, entry-level terminals and — more durably — the acquiring back end that softPOS does not remove: merchant onboarding and eKYC, terminal management systems, key injection and HSM-backed security, plus integration work for the national QR scheme, the alias register and request-to-pay. bank_theme: North Macedonia — NBG Stopanska + SEPA + deposit-ATM growth
signal: The market-level deposit-ATM story is confirmed on primary regulator data and the Stopanska picture has moved materially. NBRSM Table 3 (reference March 2026): 1,136 ATMs, up 7.0% year on year, of which 473 take cash deposits, up 16.5% year on year and up 24 in the quarter — but the total fleet has been essentially FLAT since December 2025 (1,132 / 1,132 / 1,132 / 1,136), so 2026 growth is happening INSIDE the fleet, not in unit count, and 663 machines are still dispense-only (A4). Table 5 gives the recycler economics: March 2026 ATM cash deposits 230,698 transactions worth MKD 3.65bn, up 31% by count and 53% by value, against withdrawals of 2,498,982 worth MKD 19.27bn, up 3.4% and 11.8% — deposit value is now 19.0% of withdrawal value, up from 13.8% a year earlier (A4). Branch numbers keep falling: 371 at end-2025 from 409 in 2020, down 9.3% (A4). At Stopanska specifically, H1-2026 pre-tax profit fell 30% year on year and net fee income fell 7%, which the bank attributes in its own filing to reduced payment and card tariffs AND simultaneously higher commission expenses charged by the SUPPLIERS of those services; it also completed a move into a new LEED Gold head office in Q2-2026 (A1). Its own ATM locator shows a large dispense-only tail — see the count conflict in NOTES — and its mobile app rates 2.2 out of 5 on Google Play against NLB's 3.7, the clear laggard among large-bank apps (A4). Leadership is now locked in: CEO and Board Chair Hrisula Koutoudi received a fresh four-year mandate on 18/08/2026 with NBRSM consent, CFO Mirjana Trajanovska was re-appointed to 2029 on 10/07/2026, and Zorica Božinovska-Lazarevska joined the Supervisory Board (A1, A5).

bank_theme: North Macedonia — Komercijalna banka repeatable branch-transformation template plus a 191-machine ATM estate

Its Makpetrol branch was completely modernised (reported 27/04/2026) with a DIGITAL KIOSK for commission-free utility and telecom bill payment with no teller involvement, an ATM handling deposits as well as withdrawals, and fully accessible access; the branch is staffed only 08:00-16:00 on weekdays, with the self-service devices carrying the rest. The same treatment is documented on the bank's own newsroom for at least four further sites — Novo Lisiče, Negotino, the Nabizi retail park in Struga and Avtokomanda — so this is a template, not a one-off (A4). The bank's own machine-readable ATM feed, re-pulled 27/08/2026, carries 191 records across 39 cities, 188 active, with an unpublished three-way "TypeATM" split of 98 / 82 / 11; its ATM page confirms cash withdrawal, cash deposit at labelled machines, and euro-to-denar exchange at the machine, all contactless including phone wallets, with a cash-in ceiling of 40 notes per transaction (A1). bank_theme: North Macedonia — NLB Banka Skopje digital-concept branches, contact-centre modernisation and fresh parent capital
signal: NLB Skopje is spending on physical channels and has just been given the capital to keep doing it. On 13/07/2026 it converted its "Sobranie" branch in Skopje into a 140 m2 digital-concept branch with a 24/7 self-service zone holding TWO deposit-and-withdrawal ATMs plus a separate CDS cash-deposit machine for businesses — a live cash-automation reference and a template the bank is likely to repeat (A5). Its H1-2026 filing records a new branch at Univerzalna Sala and a full reconstruction of the Dame Gruev branch in six months, and names modernisation of the business network, MODERNISATION OF THE CONTACT CENTRE, upgraded lending and payment platforms and advanced analytics as forward priorities; it launched Visa Direct real-time transfers in the half and calls itself the market's digitalisation leader (A1). Funding is in place: a EUR 10m subordinated loan from the parent qualifying as Additional Tier 1 capital (disclosed 30/07/2026), a EUR 30m long-term parent loan of which EUR 15m was drawn by 30/06/2026, a fully drawn EBRD EUR 30m green line, and MKD 2.6bn of 2025 profit retained (A1). At group level NLB's Investor Day deck states verbatim an "ATM and CDS network upgrade at Group level driving cash out of branches", with branch cash transactions down from 32% at end-2023 to 13.5% in March 2026 against a sub-10% target for 2030, and the 2026 priority list puts digital authentication and self-service legal-entity onboarding explicitly "across group" (A1). Skopje itself runs 46 branches for 469,626 active clients — 10,209 clients per branch — at a 42.8% cost-income ratio already better than the group's 46.5%, so further gains must come from channel mix (A1).

bank_theme: North Macedonia — ProCredit Bank's near-branchless model runs on 24/7 self-service zones with an ageing sub-fleet
signal: ProCredit Skopje operates the purest branch-light model in the market: as at 27/08/2026 just three full branches (Skopje-Manapo, Strumica, Bitola) plus 13 service units, with customers served through "24/7 Zones" whose confirmed capability set is unusually deep — card-controlled entry after hours, denar AND euro cash deposit and withdrawal (every zone has a euro deposit/withdrawal ATM), COIN deposit machines, daily-takings deposit either at the ATM or into a night safe using barcoded single-use security bags with magnetic-card door access, information terminals for statements, and a free direct handset to the 24/7 contact centre in every zone. Deposit capacity is 40 or 150 notes per transaction "depending on the ATM model", which is direct evidence of a mixed-generation fleet with an older sub-fleet due for replacement. The bank also runs an online branch, e-signing, OneID electronic identification, Apple and Google Pay and a PSD2 open-banking portal (A1). At group level, ProCredit Holding's Q2-2026 deck confirms North Macedonia received the new mobile retail banking app in H1-2026 and that a new business-client mobile app went live there, with digital onboarding advertised at under 15 minutes; the banking app itself is built in-house by the group's IT subsidiary Quipu, but identity, e-signature and liveness are bought from local qualified providers per market — OneID in North Macedonia — so the eKYC layer is a genuine vendor-selected slot (A1). Governance refreshed: Maja Mihajlova was re-appointed to the Management Board for four years with NBRSM consent issued 15/07/2026, and a new Supervisory Board member was appointed around 21-24/08/2026, unnamed in the published summary (A5).

bank_theme: North Macedonia — OneID national digital identity is now the live remote-onboarding rail, with three banks still outside it
signal: OneID, the national mobile electronic identity built by KIBS with Nextsense under the KibsTrust qualified-trust brand and registered as the first Macedonian eID scheme in December 2021, is now in production across essentially the whole top tier of the market. The adoption timeline from OneID's own news page: Komercijalna and Halkbank (October 2022), Sparkasse (November 2022), ProCredit and Triglav (April 2024), Silk Road Bank (September 2024), NLB Banka (March 2025), the state Central Register (June 2025) and Stopanska Banka (January 2026). The partner wall as at 27/08/2026 lists seven banks; the banks NOT on it are UNIBanka, TTK Banka and ALTA banka Bitola (A1). The scheme's own rules create a recurring workload: the electronic identity is valid for TWO YEARS and must then be renewed, it can be active on only ONE device, it requires biometric authentication on a device running at least Android 6.0 or iOS 11.4, and data updates through it are capped at ONCE PER MONTH — Stopanska runs "Client update with OneID" as a standing free service and accepts no other eID app (A1). The commercial ceiling has now moved: on 25/08/2026 Komercijalna was reported originating online consumer loans of up to MKD 2,600,000 (roughly EUR 42,000) end to end through OneID, fully remote, with immediate decision and no branch visit (A5).

implies: A national eID with a hard two-year expiry and a one-device rule creates a recurring, non-optional re-verification wave across the entire customer base of every adopting bank — the clearest digital-onboarding and eKYC opportunity in the market, plus liveness checks and an audit trail for periodic AML review. Remote origination at EUR 42,000 ticket sizes sets a competitive floor that peers must match. The once-a-month update cap throttles throughput, which is itself an argument for assisted in-branch and self-service re-verification capacity. The three banks outside the scheme are a short, precise target list. This also feeds directly into the wallet-verifier obligation in the row below, since OneID is the incumbent scheme any EU-wallet integration has to sit next to.

follow_up: Confirm the current OneID user count directly from KIBS — the 25,000 figure in circulation could not be substantiated — and establish whether OneID is being extended from KYC refresh to full remote account opening. Target UNIBanka, TTK Banka and ALTA banka Bitola for eKYC, and map the KIBS/Nextsense integration boundary before pitching anything wallet-related.

bank_theme: North Macedonia — eIDAS 2 transposed; bank wallet-verifier obligation from 01/06/2027
signal: This cycle upgrades the evidence from a consolidated-text reading to the primary bill text plus independent corroboration, and it holds. A3 re-verified the 43-page Government bill (Skopje, June 2025, proposed by Minister for Digital Transformation Stefan Andonovski) and confirms verbatim that Article 27 sets application from 1 June 2027, and that new Article 20-м(2) mirrors eIDAS Article 5f(2): private relying parties other than micro and small enterprises that require strong user authentication for online identification, in areas expressly including "банкарство, финансиски услуги" (banking, financial services), must on the user's request accept registered European digital identity wallets. Bylaws are due within six months of entry into force, and Articles 71-а to 71-в set graduated fines of EUR 500-1,000 for micro traders up to EUR 5,000-10,000 for large traders — a schedule that falls on the wallet ISSUER, not on bank relying parties. Fiscal lines: MKD 9m for 2025, MKD 200m for 2026 and MKD 200m for 2027, funded first from Digital Europe and then from the EU Growth Plan for the Western Balkans (A3). The European Commission's North Macedonia Report 2025 (04/11/2025) independently states that the law "was amended to transpose the eIDAS 2.0 Regulation and to introduce the Digital Identity Wallet" while noting existing e-identification tools are still not user-friendly or free (A3). A4 separately confirms Parliament passed the amendment among four digital-transformation reform laws at its 58th session in June 2025, and that passing the package unlocks over EUR 19m under the Reform and Growth Facility for the Western Balkans, of which EUR 5.7m is direct budget support (A4). OUTSTANDING: only the DRAFT was verified — the adopted gazette text was not obtained, so it is not proven that Article 20-м and the 01/06/2027 date survived unchanged (A3).

date: 01/06/2027 — statutory application date for bank relying parties; bylaws due within six months of entry into force; 04/11/2025 — European Commission confirms the transposing amendment was adopted
implies: If the adopted text matches the bill, North Macedonia becomes the first non-EU footprint market with a statutory bank duty to accept an EU-style identity wallet, six months before the EU's own derived acceptance date. Komercijalna, Stopanska, NLB Skopje, Halkbank, ProCredit, Sparkasse and UNIBanka must all build a wallet-verifier into digital onboarding and login, so budget has to commit from H2-2026 into H1-2027. The addressable work is the relying-party acceptance and verification layer plus remote identity proofing, HSM and key handling for relying-party keys, screening behind it because wallet identity data does not discharge full customer due diligence, and document management for retained evidence. Do not pitch on the penalty schedule — those fines fall on wallet issuers, not on banks. The six-month bylaw window is the moment to shape technical requirements with the Ministry.
likelihood: Medium-high that banks scope the work within 6-12 months — the application date is fixed in statute, but the technical specification only arrives with the ministry bylaws
follow_up: PRIORITY: obtain the ADOPTED Службен весник text and number and prove that Article 20-м and the 01/06/2027 date survived unchanged; the ministry portal and ener.gov.mk were unreachable from the collection environment. Then track the six-month bylaws and any NBRSM guidance to banks, verify the MKD 200m 2026 line against the official state budget rather than the draft-law PDF, and map the OneID integration boundary before pitching.

bank_theme: North Macedonia — Single Register of Accounts (ЕРС) + electronic forced-collection system
signal: No fresh development this cycle, and the evidence base actually weakened rather than strengthened. The obligation stands as recorded: the transitional provisions of the amended Law on Payment Services and Payment Systems (Службен весник на РСМ 144/25) require the Central Register to establish a national electronic register of denar and foreign-currency payment and deposit accounts, linked payment instruments, safe-deposit boxes, account holders, beneficial owners and legal representatives, with the Financial Intelligence Office given direct unrestricted access, and separately require an electronic forced-collection system to be established and exchanging information, with mandatory submission of forced-collection orders through it from 01/11/2027. Scope covers every NBRSM-licensed bank plus payment and e-money institutions, and no contract value is published anywhere. This cycle A3 filed no new primary work on it and explicitly flagged the deadline dates as imported from other rows without a source, while citing 30/09/2026 in two places against the master row's 01/12/2026 — so the register go-live date remains genuinely unresolved (A3).

bank_theme: North Macedonia — mandatory app-based strong authentication in force, with tokenised cards up 137%
signal: Two card-side facts now sit on regulator primary sources. First, NBRSM's own announcement confirms that from 1 March 2026 the statutory obligation on banks to apply strong customer authentication to online card payments came into force: instead of the previous SMS code, the customer receives a notification in the bank's official mobile app and must approve with the app PIN, a fingerprint or face recognition, and without that approval the payment cannot execute even if someone holds the card details. NBRSM states the obligation derives from the Law on Payment Services and Payment Systems, has been introduced in stages, already covers online account access, card payments at physical points of sale and e-/m-banking orders, and that extending it to internet payments "completes the process of alignment" with EU rules (A4). Second, NBRSM Table 2 for March 2026: 2,020,552 cards in total, up 2.7% year on year; cards with a mobile-payment (tokenised) solution 353,863 versus 148,970 a year earlier, up 137.5%, and up 21.9% in a single quarter — the fourth consecutive quarter of double-digit growth; contactless cards 1,977,099 (97.8%); and credit cards DOWN 2.5% year on year to 264,232. Growth is wallet provisioning, not new plastic. NBRSM's Q1-2026 release adds that mobile apps carry 72.8% of electronically initiated payments, themselves up 25.9%, and that each digitised card averaged only four domestic mobile transactions in the quarter (A4).

sources.text: NBRSM — Од 1 март 2026 година, побезбедни онлајн плаќања

date: 25/06/2026 — Q1-2026 card statistics published showing tokenised cards up 137.5% y/y; obligation itself in force since 01/03/2026
implies: Every Macedonian issuer now has to run app-based authentication, biometrics and cryptographic key handling across a two-million-card base of which more than 350,000 are already tokenised. That drives hardware security modules, PCI-PIN compliance and remote key injection for the provisioning and PIN estate, card-issuing and token-management work, and — because pushing authentication into the app displaces fraud from card-present toward social engineering and account takeover — behavioural transaction monitoring and fraud rules. It also gives the app-quality problem at Stopanska a plausible cause, since the token migration is compulsory and technically hard. Four transactions per digitised card per quarter is low usage, and that headroom is exactly what the national QR scheme and the instant rail are designed to unlock.
likelihood: Certain that the obligation is in force, stated by the regulator; High that tokenisation keeps compounding, having grown more than 15% quarter on quarter for four straight quarters
follow_up: Obtain the underlying NBRSM decision text from the regulations pages and check whether a transaction-risk-analysis or low-value exemption regime is defined — that is where risk engines get sold, and the press release does not mention exemptions. Pull Table 4.2 on fraudulent payment transactions for the card-not-present fraud trend that would justify the monitoring pitch; it was not checked this cycle.

bank_theme: Romania — draft law B409/2026 would force a screen-flow change on every ATM in the market inside 90 days
signal: The bill has now cleared every advisory opinion with none opposing, and the initiators' own text has been read at primary source. A new Art. 221¹ in Law 209/2019 would oblige every provider operating cash-withdrawal ATMs in Romania to let a cardholder key in a freely chosen withdrawal amount, for cards from ANY issuer authorised in Romania, and states expressly that preset fast-cash buttons do not satisfy the duty. Breach becomes a contravention fined RON 50,000–100,000 and operators get 90 days from entry into force to comply. WHAT MOVED THIS CYCLE: the National Bank of Romania's opinion no. G/161 of 17/08/2026, signed by Governor Isărescu, says the measure could improve cash access especially in rural areas and concludes that BNR "does not oppose" it — and BNR formally asked that the banking system be consulted on the technical characteristics of the terminals. The Competition Council opinion of 18/08/2026 found no competition or State-aid problem. Still first chamber, no committee report and no vote scheduled as at 27/08/2026 (A1).
date: 18/08/2026 — Competition Council opinion, the last of four, all favourable; BNR opinion 17/08/2026 does not oppose; 90-day compliance clock starts on entry into force
implies: Every ATM deployer in Romania — roughly 11,000 machines across BCR, BT, BRD, ING, Raiffeisen, UniCredit, CEC and independents including Euronet — would have to push one screen-flow change across mixed hardware and re-certify it in 90 days. No bank can procure, build, test and certify that from a standing start inside the window, which is exactly the multivendor ATM-software and managed-services proposition. Better still, the central bank has itself invited a technical consultation with the industry, so there is an open, named door to shape the specification before the text is fixed. Free-amount entry also changes the banknote mix a machine dispenses, which pulls in cash forecasting and denomination optimisation. No value is published, so it is carried unscoped.
likelihood: Medium-high that it is adopted — cross-party, urgency requested, four favourable opinions and no opposition
follow_up: Build the multivendor free-amount screen-flow package now rather than after promulgation. Ask the Romanian Banking Association to be included in the technical consultation BNR asked for — that request is on the file and is the cheapest way in. Track the Senate committee report, then the Chamber of Deputies as deciding chamber.

Because BCR hires no technology in Romania, the buying conversation runs through Erste group procurement and Erste Digital as much as through Bucharest.

bank_theme: Romania — dual ATM + POS estate expansion
signal: The acceptance mandate is the driver and it is still not verified at primary. Law 239/2025, reported as published in Monitorul Oficial no. 1160 of 15/12/2025, is reported to have amended OUG 193/2002 so that from 01/01/2026 essentially every entity registered with the Trade Register, including sole traders, must accept card or other modern electronic payment, with the previous RON 50,000 turnover threshold abolished and accepting institutions obliged to install a terminal within 30 days of request. Reported fines are RON 20,000–50,000 for failing to provide electronic acceptance and RON 5,000–7,500 for refusing a card payment. NONE of the article numbers, fine bands, the threshold repeal or the 30-day deadline could be confirmed against the Monitorul Oficial text in this cycle by any of the three agents that tried (A1, A5, A6). The circumstantial support is strong: BNR-reported terminals rose 161,396 in the second half of 2025 to 729,408, with 685,731 acceptance points and 28.63m active cards, while ATMs are reported at 11,136, up 1,108 — but the ATM jump of roughly 11% in six months is too large to be organic in a mature market and may reflect a scope change such as newly counted independent deployers, and the BNR primary page could not be reached (A1, A5). THE MARKET IS ANSWERING WITH SOFTWARE, NOT HARDWARE: banks have shipped their own softPOS apps (BCR through Global Payments' GP tom is the only one sourced), SIBS Romania completed testing of POS Sharing on softPOS on 16/07/2026, and TRANSFOND argues on its own site that a RoPay QR code can discharge the acceptance obligation — a vendor's reading of a law, not a verified legal position (A1, A6).

bank_theme: Romania — instant euro payments: banks must receive by 09/01/2027 and send with Verification of Payee by 09/07/2027
signal: The calendar is now settled at the Official Journal text after two cycles of conflicting corrections. Under Regulation (EU) No 260/2012 Art. 5a(8) as inserted by Regulation (EU) 2024/886, PSPs in non-euro Member States must offer RECEIVING of instant euro credit transfers by 09/01/2027 and SENDING by 09/07/2027; the 09/04/2027 date applies ONLY to electronic-money and payment institutions, not to banks. The same 09/01/2027 date also brings charges parity — an instant transfer may cost no more than the equivalent non-instant one — and 09/07/2027 brings mandatory VERIFICATION OF PAYEE, the payee-name-to-IBAN match (A3). Romania has already legislated: on 12/02/2026 the Government adopted an emergency ordinance amending Law 231/2015 requiring providers to settle within a MAXIMUM OF 10 SECONDS regardless of day or hour, to offer the service through ALL payment-initiation channels used by clients, to provide mandatory Verification of Payee, and — a duty the baseline missed — to report fee levels and the percentage of REJECTED TRANSACTIONS periodically to the European authorities; the ordinance also gives payment and e-money institutions access to designated payment systems. The ordinance NUMBER could not be confirmed and "OUG 5/2026" must not be cited (A3). Salt Bank ran the first local implementation of instant euro over TRANSFOND's RO-TIPS on 14/01/2026, built in about three months in partnership with TRANSFOND and MONTRAN — and Montran's own boilerplate in that release claims anti-fraud and QR products alongside instant payments, so it competes for the fraud layer too (A3, A6). Montran also holds BNR's ReGIS and SaFIR maintenance and supplied the central RoPay and instant-payments solution behind UniCredit's 02/02/2026 go-live; ten banks are live on RoPay with BRCI still in implementation (A6).
date: 09/01/2027 — Romanian banks must receive instant euro credit transfers and meet charges parity; 09/07/2027 — sending plus mandatory Verification of Payee
implies: The first hard date is roughly four months away, so budget for it is either committed or the bank is late; the commit window for the 09/07/2027 sending and Verification-of-Payee step is NOW, Q3-2026 to Q1-2027. The expensive words in the Romanian ordinance are "all payment-initiation channels" — internet banking, mobile, branch and file-based corporate channels each need instant plus name-matching — and the new rejected-transaction and fee reporting duty is a straight transaction-monitoring and regulatory-reporting requirement. The sellable layer is what Montran does not claim: instant sanctions and AML screening, deep transaction monitoring, HSM key capacity, Verification-of-Payee name-matching tuning, channel work and managed cut-over, plus the ATM and kiosk side where the free-amount bill and instant rails meet. Expect to displace rather than merely complement. The size of the remediation market is NOT established — the circulating "only four or five of about thirty Romanian PSPs are live" figure has no source and must not be used.
likelihood: High — these are fixed, directly applicable EU dates with national implementing law already adopted
follow_up: Get the ordinance from Monitorul Oficial to establish its number, the sanction levels, the competent authority and whether BNR holds any deferral power — that last point materially changes the pipeline. Get TRANSFOND's RO-TIPS participant list and onboarding calendar to replace the unsourced readiness figure with a real count. Establish which banks bought Montran and which built their own. Approach BRCI ahead of its RoPay go-live.

bank_theme: Romania — DORA and AML supervisory evidence is becoming the gate on Printec's own managed-services sales
signal: Two supervisory cycles now bear directly on whether Printec can be bought, not on what it sells. First, the DORA Register of Information: 31/12/2026 is the REFERENCE DATE, not the deadline — financial entities file to their national supervisor on that supervisor's own earlier cut-off, typically February or March 2027, and the supervisor forwards to the European supervisory authorities by 31/03/2027; the authorities do not publish the national cut-offs, so BNR must be watched individually. Only subcontractors that effectively underpin ICT services supporting critical or important functions are reportable (A3). Second, threat-led penetration testing under DORA Articles 26-27 is specified by Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2025/1190, covering scope, methodology, internal testers, remediation phases and supervisory cooperation for mutual recognition — and scope is set at entity level covering critical functions end to end, which for a retail bank pulls in the ATM channel, the acquiring and terminal estate and the monitoring layer (A3). THE ROMANIAN HOOK IS EXPLICIT: Banca Transilvania's H1-2026 risk narrative names as a board-level risk the growing dependency on third-party providers and outsourced services amid a persistent cyber threat landscape, and the bank has simultaneously pulled software development in-house (A1). Alongside these, AMLA's provisional list of entities for direct supervision is expected end-September 2026 with national supervisors having submitted by 15/08/2026, and harmonised AML sanction standards are heading to the Commission for adoption ahead of the 10/07/2027 application date (A3).

bank_theme: Serbia — NBS remote-identification rulebook (Off. Gazette 43/2026): 6- and 12-month adaptation deadlines
signal: The 21-page official decision was read in full this cycle and the picture is now precise. NBS Executive Board decision no. 14 of **07/05/2026**, published in Službeni glasnik RS 43/2026, enters into force on the eighth day after publication and outright repeals the 2019/2020/2021 regime (A1, A3). Point 33: institutions already running video identification must align business and internal acts **within six months** of entry into force and adapt their **technical solutions within one year** (A1). Point 30 adds a requirement the master row missed: any institution intending to offer video identification must notify NBS **at least 30 days before starting**, submitting internal acts, staff-training proof, the list of document-issuing states its staff are trained on, premises evidence and a full description and prior assessment of the technical solution — and must give NBS staff a **live real-time demonstration of the entire process for every customer category** before that period expires (A1). The decision creates two modes: direct (an employee on a live call) and indirect, where supervision and verification can happen before the relationship begins or, exceptionally, within 72 hours afterwards under enhanced monitoring and transaction limits (A1). **The demand picture has flipped and this is the material change:** NBS Q2-2026 data show 168,733 distance contracts concluded electronically (+25.9% y/y), of which **129,728 fully electronic (+40.6%) but only 39,005 by video identification — down 6.5% year on year, the first fall on record**, against a 2025 base year in which video-ID was the faster-growing leg at +75.4% (A4). Loan contracts drove the growth (+82.3%) while account openings fell 24.5% (A4).

bank_theme: Serbia — CReM electronic bills of exchange: statutory retail deadline 30/11/2026
signal: NBS's Annual Financial Stability Report 2025, published 05/08/2026, sets out a hard, dated compliance runway for the Central Register of Electronic Bills of Exchange (CReM). The register went live **01/12/2025**, from which date banks must enable electronic bills of exchange for legal persons and entrepreneurs; from **01/06/2026 banks are required to accept electronic bills of exchange as collateral**; and from **30/11/2026 the system must become available to natural persons**. Electronic bills are signed with a **remote qualified electronic signature via the state ConsentID app with multi-factor authentication**, and a bill can neither exist nor be transferred outside the register. NBS states explicitly that the phasing requires gradual adjustment of information systems, internal procedures and control mechanisms in banks, revision of collateral acceptance and activation procedures, and strengthening of IT security. Unlike the bank-by-bank platform models used elsewhere in the region, CReM is a single centralised NBS-operated register, so every bank integrates to the same interface (A4). Corroborating context on the same qualified-signature stack: OTP banka Srbija's August-2026 app release already uses ConsentID to sign loans above RSD 1.2m, so at least one bank has the retail plumbing in production (A1).
