bank_theme: Serbia — SEPA / instant-payments wave
signal: The regulator has now confirmed the shape of this precisely, and it is narrower than the master row assumed. NBS's own FAQ, re-read 27/08/2026, states Serbia became the 41st SEPA member on **22/05/2025** and that **18 of 19 banks** went operational on SEPA Credit Transfer on 4 and 5 May 2026 — but that Serbian banks are only in the initial phase, that all of them participate as **indirect** participants routing through correspondent parents abroad, and that **there is still no Serbian date for SEPA Instant Credit Transfer** (A3). Raiffeisen's own explainer confirms the mechanics from the bank side: credit transfer only, no 24/7 operation, working-day cycles with a maximum of next-day settlement and a 13:00 cut-off driven by its Austrian parent (A1, A5). OTP's customer article is blunter still — euro payments from Serbia to SEPA banks remain international payment traffic, executed under clearer rules rather than as domestic SEPA payments (A1). New competitive fact: **ASEE announced on 16/06/2026 that it completed SEPA implementation for 14 Serbian banks, all going live on the same day**, combining its own gateway platform with changes inside the banks' core systems (A6). The forward-looking evidence is now in the central bank's own procurement plan v9 of 26/08/2026, which carries **accession to SEPA and TIPS** and a payment-systems software upgrade to link NBS infrastructure to the EU's (A4). NBS separately plans an **ISO 20022 migration in 2026** of the Serbia–Bosnia–Montenegro FX clearing platform, a nameable set of 20 banks plus three central banks, currently exchanging SWIFT MT messages (A4). Meanwhile the domestic instant rail compounds independently: 34,459,117 instant transactions in Q2-2026, +30.7% year on year, worth RSD 442bn, with 11.3m payments in July 2026 alone at a one-second average execution time, and three banks carrying about 64% of value (A4). Serbia is aligning to PSD2, not PSD3 — three draft laws went to consultation in late May and early June 2026 (A3).

bank_theme: Serbia — cash-in, not cash-out, is where the ATM channel is growing
signal: The Q2-2026 regulator series, published 19/08/2026, moves every number in the master row and strengthens the argument. The national estate reached **3,412 ATMs and 195,121 POS terminals at 30/06/2026**, up from 3,336 and 187,957 at Q1-2026 and 3,196 and 177,185 a year earlier — **+216 ATMs (+6.8%) and +17,936 POS (+10.1%) year on year**, plus 6,278 virtual points of sale (+21.4%) and 13.7m cards issued to 7.1m users (A1, A4, A5). That +6.8% is **the highest year-on-year ATM growth in the whole published NBS series back to Q1-2016** (A4). Against that, **ATM cash-deposit transactions reached 3,406,129 worth RSD 173.9bn in Q2-2026, +31.9% by count and +53.6% by value year on year, while withdrawals grew just +4.5% by count and +15.7% by value** — so deposit value is now 31.5% of withdrawal value, up from 23.7% a year earlier, and deposits are 11% of ATM transaction count but 24% of ATM transaction value (A1, A4, A5). Cash withdrawal at the branch teller **fell 3.9%** (A5). On the wider cash series, deposit value has run at 1.4 to 1.5 times withdrawal value since 2024, and in H1-2026 withdrawal value went flat year on year (+0.4%) while withdrawal count fell 5.8% — so cash out is no longer growing even in nominal terms while cash in still is (A4). Card purchases at Serbian merchants hit 237.9m in Q2-2026, +19.3% year on year and more than double the Q2-2022 figure (A1, A4). The branch base is going the other way: NBS told the press in May 2026 that bank organisational units fell from 1,558 in March 2021 to **1,288 in March 2026**, a 17.3% cut, with sector headcount down to 21,732 (A4). Bank-level disclosures corroborate the same migration independently — 86% of Banca Intesa's dinar deposits and 97% of Raiffeisen's Premium-segment cash transactions already happen on machines (A1).

implies: This is the single set of numbers that underwrites every Serbian self-service proposal and should be the first slide in all of them, now with a stronger version of the same claim: Serbia is one of the very few European markets **adding** ATMs, at the fastest rate in a decade, while a branch network 17% smaller than five years ago pushes cash onto the machines. Money going into ATMs is growing roughly three and a half times faster in value than money coming out, and a near one-to-one deposit-to-withdrawal ratio is precisely the condition under which recycling beats separate deposit and dispense machines and starts cutting cash-in-transit journeys and vault holdings. A dispense-only machine is therefore a depreciating asset regardless of fleet size. Two disciplines: the ATM upturn is only three or four quarters old, so present it as a trend rather than a guarantee; and NBS publishes no split of the 3,412 machines by deposit or recycling capability, so any deposit-capable share must be built bottom-up from bank locator feeds.
likelihood: High — structural and consistent across six consecutive quarters and corroborated by bank-level disclosure
follow_up: Standardise a one-page Serbian market slide on the deposit-versus-withdrawal divergence plus the branch-network contraction, and attach it to every bank-level proposal. Build a Serbia-specific recycling return-on-investment model off the NBS deposit and withdrawal volumes and take it to the top five banks. Ask the NBS Payment System Department whether deposit and recycling-capable ATMs can be broken out on request, and write to Bank Supervision for the post-2019 organisational-unit and employee series, which they demonstrably still hold. Refresh both workbooks each quarter.

bank_theme: Serbia — the incumbent competitor set is now named: Payten/ASEE, Mellon and MoneyGet
signal: Three separate evidence types converge on a clear competitive map. **Payten (Asseco SEE) is entrenched and locally incorporated through four Serbian legal entities** — Payten d.o.o. Beograd, Chip Card a.d. Belgrade, Afusion and Monri Payments — with a catalogue that overlaps almost line for line: ATM infrastructure and outsourcing, multivendor ATM maintenance, ATM software, cardless cash, softPOS, POS infrastructure and software, acquiring and issuing processing, tokenisation and transaction monitoring (A1). Its **MoneyGet independent ATM network was re-counted at 198 unique locations in Serbia on 27/08/2026**, about 5.8% of the national estate, run on a no-capex partner model that recruits site owners with free installation and maintenance — chasing exactly the off-premise sites a challenger would target (A1). In the public register Payten holds **38 Serbian public contracts**, including the Office for IT and eGovernment's POS system usage service at RSD 10.0m for 12 months from **20/01/2026 — so a renewal falls due around January 2027** — plus a payment-gateway upgrade, the card-payment device estates of Belgrade's public parking and garage operators, and a small POS order at the central bank (A2). **But the group has publicly conceded a retreat in hardware:** ASEE's H1-2026 management report of 31/07/2026 shows the Payment Solutions segment down 5% to EUR 102.8m, with the ATM line down EUR 3.4m attributed explicitly to *lower equipment deliveries in South-Eastern Europe, particularly in Serbia, Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina and Montenegro*, and the POS line down EUR 1.9m — while the independent-terminal-network and fiscal-cash-register lines grew EUR 2.7m and independent-network transactions rose 41% year on year (A6). Serbia remains ASEE's largest country at EUR 53.8m revenue (+13%) and EUR 8.5m EBIT (+33%), so this is a shift from box sales to a recurring annuity book, not a withdrawal (A6). Separately, **Mellon Serbia has stacked three Serbian bank relationships inside twelve months** — Ingenico terminals at Raiffeisen (20/08/2025), a queue-management rollout across 60-plus OTP branches (18/02/2026) and POS acquiring at ProCredit (12/02/2026) — making it the most active non-Payten challenger and putting it inside two priority accounts (A6). Euronet, by contrast, named **no new European ATM-outsourcing win at all** on its Q2-2026 call of 30/07/2026, while running a sustained total-cost-of-ownership campaign aimed at bank finance directors (A6).
date: 31/07/2026 — ASEE's H1-2026 report discloses falling ATM and POS deliveries naming Serbia first among the affected markets · 27/08/2026 MoneyGet's Serbian network re-counted at 198 locations · eGovernment POS contract renewal falls due ~January 2027
implies: The dominant regional rival has put in writing that its Serbian ATM hardware deliveries shrank in the first half of 2026 while its recurring service book grew — which is a real displacement window on hardware refresh and estate modernisation, but not on the whole relationship, and it should be framed that way. Its order backlog shows contracted revenue flat to down while contracted margin rises, the signature of a company taking fewer, better-priced deals, which means autumn 2026 is the moment to test firm rather than defensive pricing. The genuine structural threat is not ATMs at all: it is the independent terminal network growing 41% a year, where a single device replaces several acquirer terminals and moves the terminal relationship away from the bank entirely. Meanwhile Mellon is encroaching on two accounts from the POS and queue-management side, one step from bidding self-service work at renewal, and Euronet's cost-of-ownership campaign is the argument that will appear in every Serbian self-service bid over the next year, written for finance rather than technology.
likelihood: Standing competitive condition; the concrete near-term events are the January-2027 eGovernment renewal and the ASEE Q3 disclosure on 26/10/2026
follow_up: Build a written counter-model to the ATM-as-a-service total-cost-of-ownership argument that concedes each cost category — connectivity, compliance and software upgrades, lifecycle management, cash availability — and shows each is addressable without surrendering the estate, naming a local cash-transport partner on every bid so the risk-transfer gap is visibly closed. Ask Printec Serbia which Payten-supplied ATM contracts fall due in 2026-27. Establish whether Mellon's Raiffeisen and ProCredit scope includes terminal management and field service or is hardware supply only. Re-read the ASEE Q3 report on 26/10/2026 to see whether the ATM retreat is structural. Track the independent-terminal-network transaction count quarterly as the proxy for how fast bank-owned terminal estates are being displaced.

bank_theme: Serbia — public-sector cash automation and kiosks are held by named local incumbents
signal: A sweep of the national procurement register identifies who actually holds Serbian public cash-handling work, and it is not a flat layer of price-only dealers. **Master Team d.o.o. (PIB 100093505)** is bank-grade: as the joint bidder group 'Master Team Olimp-ex' it holds the National Bank of Serbia's **automatic banknote sorting and packing systems** under two contracts both dated 05/02/2024, RSD 206,546,000 and RSD 7,072,000 excluding VAT — a combined **RSD 213.6m, roughly EUR 1.8m**, both recorded as fully paid and completed. It also supplies NBS control note-counting machines (most recently RSD 768,000 on 07/10/2025), Pošta Srbije, the Customs Administration and a steady stream of municipal utilities through 2026, the latest on 11/08/2026 (A2). **Vivex Group d.o.o. (PIB 100828591)** is the second tier-one player and holds the state Treasury's whole stack: multifunction vault counting and sorting machines at RSD 8.3m (23/09/2025), money-banding machines at RSD 3.99m (02/03/2026) and safe and vault repair at RSD 4.0m signed 10/07/2026 — most of them on single or two-bid fields (A2). On the kiosk side, **Inova Tech d.o.o. and Elektro Energy d.o.o.** took the Velika Plana municipal self-service kiosk contract for paying administrative fees at RSD 17,973,000 (~EUR 153k), signed 15/06/2026 on a single bid, classified as works rather than goods so installation and site power were in scope (A2). Other named incumbents at NBS: exceet Card Schweiz AG on DataCard personalisation service, Latis d.o.o. on vault doors and the Taurunum pair on manned guarding to 2029 (A2). **Verification caveat:** the vendor agent re-fetched the tender headers on 31/08/2026 and confirmed each procurement exists with the stated subject and status, but could **not** independently re-verify the contract values, winner names or signature dates, because the portal serves a JavaScript shell and returns 401 on its data paths without credentials (A6).

implies: The Serbian public cash-automation market has two technically qualified defenders, not a soft dealer layer, and one of them has already delivered a multi-million-euro automatic sorting installation to the central bank. That reframes entry strategy entirely: the realistic routes are to partner with or acquire one of the two for local service reach, or to bid the next central-bank automatic-sorting cycle directly on qualification and service depth rather than assuming an incumbent can be out-specified on price. The kiosk award carries a second lesson — the winning structure for Serbian municipal work is an integrator paired with a local civils-and-power firm, so Elektro Energy is better treated as a candidate installation partner than a competitor, and the bank segment should be defended on what a municipal kiosk supplier typically cannot offer: cash-accepting and recycling kiosks, certified card acceptance, device telemetry and monitored field service.

(PIB 100093505) properly and establish **which banknote-processing manufacturer it represents on the NBS sorting and packing systems** — that single answer determines whether an existing manufacturer partnership is a wedge or a blocked door — and identify the 'Olimp-ex' partner in the bidder group. bank_theme: Slovakia — eKasa cashless mandate + deposit-ATM expansion
signal: The statutory duty to let customers pay cashlessly on any sale above EUR 1 is live and the legal detail is now nailed down at the primary text. Act 384/2025 Z. z. took effect 01/01/2026 and its section 15(1) acceptance duty applied from 01/05/2026 after Act 30/2026 Z. z. postponed it from 01/03/2026 (A1, A2). NEW THIS CYCLE — (a) section 15(3) expressly allows a THIRD PARTY to supply the technical means that confirm a QR-code payment back to the cash register, an explicit statutory opening for a private vendor to run the payment-confirmation layer, with the technical specification a legal duty the Financial Directorate had still not published at 27/08/2026; (b) the sanction ladder is far harder than previously reported — first detection is a formal instruction only, second carries EUR 500-15,000, each further detection EUR 3,000-40,000, and section 17(5)-(6) class it a "particularly serious breach" that can cost the merchant its trade licence; (c) on the Financial Directorate register of valid certifications at 19/08/2026 Printec Slovakia holds decision 322095/2025 for "Printec eKasa Service verzia 1.2" effective to at most 20/06/2030, but the register carries 65 decisions across 38 companies, so certification is a qualifier to compete, not a differentiator, and Diebold Nixdorf holds two of its own decisions plus supplies the protected data store into a third party's certified stack; (d) the regulator confirms two recurring merchant-side replacement cycles — eKasa credentials expire every 2 years and the protected data store fills and must be swapped every 2-6 years — while the 5-year certification clock binds only the manufacturer and must NOT be sold to merchants as a forced replacement. The QR-code alternative means the smallest merchants can comply with no hardware, which caps terminal upside and favours SoftPOS. The reported jump from 70,943 to 77,711 POS terminals could NOT be verified this cycle and must not be quoted.

implies: The largest single POS and acquiring trigger in Slovakia, realised entirely through private merchants and acquirers and therefore invisible on the public-procurement portal. Three things to sell: SoftPOS plus terminal management at the un-terminalised micro-merchant tail; a certified third-party QR payment-confirmation service once the Financial Directorate publishes the specification; and a managed service around credential renewal and protected-data-store swaps for the installed base, which is a genuine recurring annuity rather than a one-off box sale.
likelihood: High — the duty is in force and the live variable is the enforcement ramp through 2026-27
follow_up: Size the un-terminalised merchant tail and pitch SoftPOS plus terminal management to Slovak acquirers, positioned against the QR carve-out rather than against the mandate. Watch financnasprava.sk for the section 15(3) technical specification — publication is a legal duty and therefore a datable trigger. Get the terminal count from NBS payment statistics before quoting any figure to a client.

bank_theme: Slovenská pošta — self-service kiosks + EUR 1.75m security managed services
signal: The EUR 1,745,311.25 / 36-month contract for higher-level support of the information-security systems across Slovak Post's IT estate is STILL OPEN and the deadline has MOVED TWICE — from 14/08/2026 to 08/09/2026 10:00 (opening 10:30), by correction notice 11298-IOX of 06/08/2026, republished on TED as 542285-2026. Two clarifications that change the bid team: the scope is information-security operations (administration, maintenance, monitoring, testing and further development), NOT physical guarding; and bids go through Slovak Post's own ERANET portal at posta.eranet.sk, not JOSEPHINE or EVO. The sole award criterion is lowest price excluding VAT, so the decision is entirely cost base. Two further developments at the same buyer: a EUR 13,692,340 / 48-month logistics information system covering the branch and BalíkoBOX estate CLOSED 24/08/2026 and is in evaluation with no award published — the winner becomes the systems integrator any later counter or self-service work must route through; and the BalíkoBOX parcel-locker field-maintenance framework was awarded to KOVAL SYSTEMS a.s. at EUR 1,957,059.50 for 24 months on a SINGLE bid within EUR 62 of the estimate, which is direct evidence that Slovak Post has no competitive field-service market for self-service terminals (A2, A6). The five-branch self-service cash-kiosk pilot still has not converted into a procurement and no incumbent is locked in.
date: 08/09/2026 10:00 — extended bid deadline for the EUR 1.75m security-support tender; logistics IS closed 24/08/2026 awaiting award; BalíkoBOX framework runs to ~May 2028
implies: The most accessible openings in Slovakia sit at one buyer. A EUR 1.75m three-year support annuity is biddable for another week and awarded purely on price, which favours a regional cost base. The BalíkoBOX single-bid award is the clearest read-across in the market to Printec's own book — Printec already maintains Pošta Slovenije's parcel lockers next door — and points at a ~May 2028 re-tender with no competitive tension to overcome. The unconverted kiosk pilot remains the one self-service opening at Slovak Post with no incumbent.
likelihood: High — one deadline inside days and two further awards due Q4 2026
follow_up: Make the bid or no-bid call before 08/09/2026 and register on posta.eranet.sk, not JOSEPHINE. Watch ÚVO tender 561100 for the logistics IS winner, who becomes the gatekeeper for branch technology. Approach Slovak Post now with the Pošta Slovenije locker reference and ask for the ~2028 BalíkoBOX market consultation, and separately push to convert the five-branch kiosk pilot.

bank_theme: Národná banka Slovenska — core-banking pre-RFP + ageing cash estate
signal: The core-banking replacement (CORBS) is STILL pre-procurement — two market consultations have run, the most recent in April 2025, and a sweep of every NBS notice from 06/07/2026 to 27/08/2026 found no CORBS tender. What is genuinely new is that the central bank's cash-equipment cycle is now DATED rather than merely described. An exhaustive sweep of all 465,236 notices in the ÚVO archive shows the ATM category has never carried a single Slovak notice, and banknote and coin equipment only four and two respectively. The winners are now named: NBS's banknote-processing contract went to Giesecke+Devrient Currency Technology GmbH, signed 06/05/2019, EUR 6,519,820 excluding VAT on a SINGLE bid, covering ten machines with integrated shredders plus warranty and EIGHT YEARS of post-warranty service — i.e. expiring around mid-2027; the coin processing and packaging lines went to QEX a.s. of Trenčín, EUR 1,589,050.07, with ten years of service. In parallel NBS awarded HICO s.r.o. a four-year, EUR 298,198.80 construction-supervision framework on 15/07/2026 for its PERMANENT BACKUP SITE at Kremnica, which dates the main works and the vault, cash-handling, physical-security and IT fit-out procurements to roughly 2027-28 (A2). Reinforcing the direction of travel, NBS has just committed up to EUR 56.25m of collector-coin minting frameworks to the Kremnica Mint through ~2030, and the ECB opened its public vote on ten shortlisted new euro banknote designs on 23/07/2026 with a Governing Council decision due around end-2026, which will eventually force recognition-sensor and note-template upgrades across every note-handling machine in the country (A6).

The euro banknote redesign adds a recognition-upgrade annuity behind both. CORBS remains unclaimed but is most plausibly approached through a local partner rather than as a prime bid.

bank_theme: Národná banka Slovenska — integration platform, tender notice expected 14/09/2026

bank_theme: Slovakia — commercial-bank deposit-ATM and recycler build-out
signal: The best-evidenced hardware cycle in the cluster, and this cycle it acquired a much harder denominator and a new driver. HARD COUNTS: Slovenská sporiteľňa's H1-2026 disclosures state 733 ATMs including 296 deposit machines — the largest network in Slovakia — meaning roughly 437 machines are cash-out only and deposit penetration is already 40.4%, not the third previously assumed; the fleet SHRANK from 752 to 733 in six months while branches fell 140 to 128, so branches are contracting about 3.4 times faster than machines (A1, 30/07/2026). VÚB publishes 150 deposit ATMs, banknotes only, with a 50-note versus 200-note per-deposit split that is a clear hardware-generation tell, inside a network it is holding EXACTLY flat at 163 outlets while headcount falls — automation inside the branch, not closure (A1, 28/07/2026). ČSOB Slovakia's own list carries 124 deposit machines at 99 addresses, of which 66 accept coins, but only 23 addresses are off-branch (A1, 27/08/2026). Tatra banka runs 355 deposit machines handling ~450,000 deposits a month, and seven Slovak banks now operate deposit ATMs across a national estate of roughly 1,000 (A5). NEW DRIVER: as at 17/08/2026 branch cash desks are being dismantled across all five large banks — SLSP 93 of 128 branches with no cash desk, Tatra 48 of 69, ČSOB 47 of 120, VÚB 25 of 121, UniCredit 16 of 47 — with the banks themselves naming security regimes, staff training and vault equipment as the cost they are escaping (A5). Erste's group disclosures show Slovakia taking the DEEPEST branch cut in the group, 150 to 128 in twelve months. Coin deposit is absent from SLSP's and VÚB's published propositions, so a coin offer has no incumbent product to displace.

date: 17/08/2026 — cash-desk removal quantified across all five large banks; SLSP H1-2026 fleet and deposit counts published 30/07/2026
implies: Every closed cash desk has to be replaced by a recycler or deposit machine in the branch lobby, and the banks have stated the pain themselves in exactly the terms a managed cash service answers. VÚB at 25 of 121 and UniCredit at 16 of 47 are the least converted and therefore the largest remaining retrofit pipelines; ČSOB Slovakia at 47 of 120 is third. At SLSP the pitch has to shift: at 40% deposit penetration it is refresh, managed services and the ~437 cash-out-only machines, not greenfield deposit capability. Coin handling is open white space at both of the market's largest banks. None of this is procured publicly — Slovak retail banks are private and outside procurement law — so it is a direct commercial sale.
likelihood: High — the conversion is on the record and running at five banks simultaneously
follow_up: Build a branch-by-branch conversion model for VÚB and ČSOB Slovakia and lead with total cost of cash rather than hardware price. Take SLSP a refresh and managed-services case built on displaced transactions per closed branch, and pull its published deposit-ATM list to geo-map the ~437-machine upgrade backlog. Test coin-deposit appetite with SLSP's business cash-handling team.

bank_theme: ČSOB Slovakia / 365.bank / Poštová banka — ~600-machine shared ATM network heading into a legal merger
signal: ČSOB Slovakia's own press release of 03/06/2026 states that from 01/07/2026 clients of ČSOB, 365.bank and Poštová banka can use a combined network of nearly 600 ATMs on their own bank's terms, with the previous EUR 200 cross-bank withdrawal cap abolished; ČSOB contributes 428 machines and 365.bank 176. The arrangement covers WITHDRAWALS ONLY — ČSOB's deposit machines stay closed to the other two banks' customers. A legal merger of the two banks was planned for autumn 2026 (A5). KBC's own 2Q2026 quarterly report independently confirms the corporate side and resolves what A5 could not source: the 98.45% acquisition of 365.bank from J&T Finance Group completed on 15/01/2026 for EUR 708m, generating EUR 176m of goodwill, consolidated from January 2026, adding EUR 3,647m to the Slovak loan book, and justified in part by "significant cost synergies related to the branch network and head office in Slovakia"; 365.bank's distribution rests on a long-standing partnership with Slovak Post; integration costs were booked as exceptional in 2Q2026 (A1, 06/08/2026).
date: 06/08/2026 — KBC restates the completed acquisition and the branch-network cost-synergy case; shared 600-machine network live since 01/07/2026; legal merger planned autumn 2026
implies: This is the largest single ATM rationalisation and refresh decision in the Slovak market. Two overlapping estates and two self-service fleets have to be consolidated, duplicate sites removed, surviving sites standardised onto one platform, and a postal-counter channel brought onto that platform — with an explicitly stated branch cost-synergy target driving it. The unsolved problem is deposit interoperability, which needs recyclers and cross-bank deposit switching. The integration clock started in January 2026, so the target operating model is being set now.
likelihood: High that a network and channel rationalisation programme runs through 2026-27; vendor choices likely tied to ČSOB and KBC group frameworks
follow_up: Get in front of the ČSOB Slovakia integration programme office before the merger fixes the target operating model. Confirm whether the legal merger completed in autumn 2026, obtain the combined estate plan and the deposit-interoperability roadmap, and identify the incumbent ATM vendor on each of the two fleets and whether 365.bank's Slovak Post counters carry their own machines.

bank_theme: Slovakia — cross-bank deposit-ATM interoperability, still at the analysis stage with no vendor locked in

bank_theme: Slovenia — draft Cash Access Act sets a statutory ATM density floor
signal: **The bill is alive and now in direct negotiation with the banks, but its headline density numbers have become formally contested.** The Ministry of Finance closed the public consultation on the draft **Zakon o dostopnosti in uporabi plačilnih sredstev (ZDUPS) on 17/08/2026 with 23 written responses**; the ministry's own release records respondents proposing "different or new criteria for the cash-point network", wider exemptions from mandatory cash acceptance, removal of the electronic-payment-acceptance duty into a separate procedure, and a longer adaptation period. On **24/08/2026 the ministry met the Banka Slovenije working group and the Bank Association of Slovenia (ZBS)** and said it will continue "constructive dialogue with the banks" — no decisions, no revised criteria, no timetable. **An ECB opinion under Art. 127(4) TFEU is still outstanding**, and the bill has not reached a government session or the Državni zbor as at 31/08/2026 (A3, A5). **Verification conflict this cycle:** A5 reports the density obligations as confirmed in a summary published by the municipalities' association ZMOS — at least 60 ATMs per 100,000 inhabitants, 95% of the population within 5 km, an ATM within 5 km of settlements above 1,000 people, a branch or post office within 5 km for settlements above 3,000, at most 3% substitutable by cashback or cash-in-shop, plus a merchant duty to accept at least one electronic payment instrument — while A3 re-read the ministry's own releases and found **none of those figures appear there and could not be verified against the bill text**. The bill pairs the access-to-cash mandate with a **free basic payment-services package** for everyone receiving salaries, pensions or other regular income, which the ZBS calls problematic in principle and which press reporting says may draw a constitutional-court challenge. Field context (press-tier): NLB now 69 branches and 508 ATMs against 113 and 558 ten years ago; OTP banka Slovenije 71 branches and 400 ATMs against a combined NKBM plus SKB 126 and 493. In parallel the EU **Legal Tender of Cash Regulation moved into trilogue** — ECON voted to open negotiations 23/06/2026, confirmed by plenary 08/07/2026 — which would put an EU floor under the same obligation with no published conclusion date.

bank_theme: NLB d.d. — ATM accessibility retrofit to 2030 under the Slovenian accessibility act
signal: **The accessibility act was amended and the amendment turns accessibility into a procurement gate, which the master row did not capture.** The Zakon o spremembah in dopolnitvah Zakona o dostopnosti do proizvodov in storitev za invalide (**ZDPSI-A**) was passed on 11/02/2026, published in Uradni list RS 14/2026 on 24/02/2026 and **in force since 25/02/2026**. The commercially decisive change is a new Art. 3(5) providing verbatim that the accessibility conditions "constitute mandatory accessibility requirements which are taken into account in public procurement procedures when drawing up the technical specifications of the contract". Also new: the market-surveillance inspectorate **TIRS must take immediate restrictive measures including withdrawal of a product from the market**; an operator invoking disproportionate burden must notify the surveillance bodies; the minister may prescribe functional-performance criteria as an alternative to technical conditions; self-service terminals lawfully in use before 28/06/2025 may run to the end of their economic life but **no longer than 20 years** from entry into use; and Art. 18(5) lets a contracting authority amend **live** tender documents to apply the new rule where the deadline has not passed (A3). Carried forward and still valid: NLB Group's Annual Report 2025 states that 58 ATMs in Slovenia support voice-guided transactions for blind and partially sighted customers with 26 more due by Q1-2026, against a group commitment to equip **all** ATMs by **2030**; press-tier field data this cycle puts NLB's Slovenian fleet at **508 ATMs**, so several hundred machines remain to upgrade (A5). The master row's verifier correction stands: Banka Slovenije has **not** asked payment service providers for accessibility plans, and its National Payments Council minutes of 21/03/2025 closed the topic.

Second, the two Slovenian bills interlock: if any density floor survives the cash-access act, NLB, OTP banka Slovenije and Pošta must **add** cash points and every added machine must be accessible from day one with no legacy derogation. At NLB itself the work stays a deadline-bound fleet programme — audio and accessibility hardware kits, voice-guidance ATM software and nationwide field-service execution across several hundred machines — but with no supervisory prompt, so timing follows the ordinary fleet cycle and the target is the 2027 hardware plan.

Independently, the Slovenian market is visibly hiring for exactly the capability the evaluators say is missing: **Addiko Slovenia was running a simultaneous three-role data cluster — data engineer, data governance analyst and data analyst — plus two group market and liquidity risk roles**, and Delavska hranilnica posted a data-governance specialist on 25/08/2026 (A5). Carried forward and still valid: NLB's own technology deck names "AI at scale: AML, retail credit risk, chatbots" as a board-level programme.

The demand case is nonetheless the strongest in the country: the NBU branch register at 01/07/2026 shows Oschadbank running **1,115 operating structural subdivisions, by far the largest estate in Ukraine, down only 16 (-1.4%) in H1-2026** — so it is not consolidating its way out of teller cost — **plus 640 temporarily suspended subdivisions**, a dormant pool larger than any private bank's whole network (A1, A4). It also carries, with PrivatBank, Raiffeisen and PUMB, a **statutory duty to exchange the withdrawn 1, 2, 5 and 10 hryvnia notes free and without limit until 28/02/2029**, while ordinary banks shed the duty on 26/02/2027 — regulator-mandated manual teller work in a network it is keeping (A1). Affordability has worsened: **H1-2026 net profit fell 2.9x to UAH 3.38bn**, dropping the bank from second to fourth in the sector, against total assets of UAH 518.87bn, with a 50% temporary bank corporate tax rate in force and UAH 4.8bn of dividends paid to the state budget (A1). Two further access points: Oschadbank went live as an open-banking ASPSP on 03/08/2026, and it is one of the 26 banks in the NBU's 2026 resilience assessment (A1, A5).
date: 25/08/2026 — first safes lot awarded at 48.7% below estimate; second lot pending. Context: H1-2026 profit down 2.9x reported 14/08/2026; branch register at 01/07/2026
implies: Oschadbank is buying **safes**, which are the manual alternative to a teller cash recycler, and buying them transactionally on price from single local bidders — so a hardware-only pitch will lose and a long education cycle should be expected. The commercially correct framing is the opposite of PrivatBank's: Raiffeisen is shrinking hard and needs self-service to displace counters, whereas Oschadbank is **holding a 1,115-branch footprint and needs efficiency inside it**, with a statutory small-note exchange duty running to 2029 that guarantees manual counter volume. A bank whose profit fell threefold will sign opex, not capex — so lead with cash automation inside a managed-service wrapper, and use the 04/09/2026 banknote work as the non-discretionary entry point.
likelihood: Medium — the buyer is active and accessible but is currently in a low-tech, price-led buying pattern with no self-service line visible
follow_up: Use the named branch-equipment procurement desk that ran both safes lots as the entry point for a teller-cash-recycler and branch-transformation pitch. Register Printec Ukraine on Oschadbank's Prozorro procurements and monitor its ATM and security categories. Open on the 04/09/2026 banknote reconfiguration and the open-banking security layer rather than on safes. Note the bank's own site sits behind an Imperva challenge, so its H1-2026 interim, capex line and ATM count still need a browser session or a direct ask.

bank_theme: Ukrposhta — POS estate + CIT outsourcing; Printec already qualified

bank_theme: NBU — UAH 2,000 banknote fleet reconfiguration (~38,700 devices, Aug–Dec 2026)
signal: The device population is now confirmed from the **NBU's own data file rather than press**, and a second dated regulatory workstream has opened. The **UAH 2,000 note (Vasyl Stus, 75x166 mm) enters circulation on 04/09/2026** — an entirely new highest denomination, and the NBU's banknotes-in-circulation page still lists only 1000/500/200/100/50/20, confirming it is not yet in issue (A1, A4). Exact estate at 01/07/2026 from NBU PC_table_1.xlsx: **38,721 self-service devices — 15,768 ATMs and 22,953 PTKS self-service payment kiosks** (38,685 at 01/06/2026) (A4). The NBU is giving banks, cash-in-transit firms and device service companies **free technical configuration capability during August 2026**, and states this is the **first time it has run such a procedure before a banknote's circulation date**, because the materials cannot be released until the note is declassified at presentation (A4). Separately and new this cycle: on **26/08/2026 the NBU opened consultation on amendments to the Instruction on organising bank cash operations**, driven expressly by preparation for the new denomination — adding it to the list of notes banks must surrender to the NBU and refining the uniform packaging-material specifications for 2,000-hryvnia notes; **written comments close 04/09/2026 inclusive** (A1). Note the scope limit honestly: that particular resolution covers surrender lists and packaging, so the validator and recycler work is a **commercial consequence** of the new note, not something this resolution mandates. Because the fleet is 59% PTKS kiosks rather than bank ATMs, the work lands heavily on independent kiosk operators such as EasyPay, iBox and City24, which have thinner engineering benches than banks (A4).
date: 04/09/2026 — the note enters circulation, and the same day comments close on the NBU's cash-operations amendments. Free configuration materials opened August 2026; the reconfiguration itself runs on past the circulation date
implies: A hard-dated, market-wide field-services and firmware event across roughly 38,700 devices: note-template and firmware updates on every acceptor, dispenser, recycler and back-office sorter, cassette re-planning, denomination-mix changes in cash forecasting, and device-by-device verification. Because a new **highest** denomination changes cassette mix and replenishment economics, it is also a cash-forecasting re-tuning trigger. The commercial framing is not a 04/09 cliff but a race that starts on 04/09 and is won on speed and verified per-device coverage — the laggards after the date are the retrofit pipeline.
likelihood: Certain — the note enters circulation 04/09/2026 and the device counts are from the NBU's own file
follow_up: Retrieve the NBU draft resolution, impact analysis and comparison table posted 26/08/2026 for the exact packaging specifications, and file or track comments before 04/09/2026. Establish which note-set and firmware versions NCR Atleos, Glory, Sesami and the bill-validator vendors have released for the UAH 2,000 note. From 05/09/2026 chase which banks and which PTKS operators still cannot accept or dispense it — that list is the pipeline. Also test whether the 6 mm length delta forces any cassette hardware change; no source currently says it does.

bank_theme: NBU Resolution No. 67 — mandatory one-time-password identity capture at self-service cash-in terminals
signal: Re-verified **line by line against the official 9-page NBU PDF** this cycle, and now sized against the exact device count. Resolution No. 67 of 16/06/2026, officially published 18/06/2026, **in force 26/06/2026**. New clause 124-2 requires, for **every cash-in at a self-service payment kiosk regardless of amount**, that the payer key their full mobile number on the kiosk screen and that the provider or its commercial agent verify ownership of that number by a one-time password sent by SMS or read out by phone call, which the payer then keys on the kiosk screen. Clause 124-3 obliges the provider — including where commercial agents are used — to take **continuous** measures making it impossible or lower-risk to pass the password to another person, **including shortening its validity**. Clause 124-4 carries a **materially longer exemption list than first reported**: budget payments (taxes, fines, administrative-service fees), utilities under the Housing-Services Law plus fixed telephony, TV, internet and security, rail tickets including suburban, urban and suburban transport fares including e-tickets, route passenger transport, transport-card top-ups, mobile-service payments within the provider up to UAH 500 per month per number, and cash-in to top up an account with an issued payment instrument. The resolution also sets cash-work rules for the new financial-inclusion bank licence type and its commercial agents (A4). Scope: **22,953 PTKS kiosks at 01/07/2026** each need a screen-flow change plus SMS or voice OTP integration (A4).
date: 26/06/2026 — in force; a non-compliant terminal may not execute the cash-in at all. Re-verified against the official PDF and sized at 22,953 kiosks as at 01/07/2026
implies: Every cash-in kiosk in Ukraine needs a new screen flow, an SMS or voice one-time-password integration, and remote rollout across a fleet nobody can visit machine by machine — which is a terminal-management job, not a site visit. Clause 124-3 makes password-sharing (money-mule) risk a **standing legal duty**, so it is a rules-and-monitoring requirement rather than a one-off interface patch. The broad exemption list cuts both ways: operators will want conditional branching rather than a blanket prompt, which is more integration work, not less.
likelihood: In force since 26/06/2026 — the remediation demand is immediate, and the ban on executing the payment makes non-compliance an outage rather than a project
follow_up: Ask EasyPay, iBox and City24 directly how they implemented the OTP step and the exemption branching, and whether the NBU has begun enforcement — the independent operators are the ones most likely to be short. Approach banks on the receipt-retention and monitoring feed rather than only the terminal interface, and combine the pitch with the UAH 2,000 note reconfiguration, since both land on the same 22,953 kiosks in the same quarter.

bank_theme: NBU Resolution No. 81 — customer verification methods widened for financial inclusion
signal: **The master row's headline needs correcting.** Two agents independently re-verified Resolution No. 81 of 15/07/2026 against the NBU's own notice of 16/07/2026 and the official legal portal, and **neither found the geolocation, geotagging, photo-metadata-timestamp or no-editing requirements** the master row leads with (A3, A4). What is confirmed is different and narrower: the resolution amends the Regulation on banks' financial monitoring (Regulation No. 65 of 19/05/2020), entered into force **17/07/2026**, and (a) permits the original identity document to be presented during verification by a **third party — an accompanying or authorised person — or handled by the verifying bank employee** where the client cannot present it unaided, and (b) permits the client's consent to photo capture to be evidenced by **audio or video recording** where a handwritten or electronic signature is impossible. Separately, under the financial-inclusion law, the new **financial-inclusion bank** licence type may engage a **commercial agent** to establish the beneficiary of a transaction and to carry out identification and verification under the same regulation; the NBU adopted the surrounding regulatory package for this institution type in June 2026 (A3, A4). The master row's other elements — Diia e-passport and electronic taxpayer card acceptance including QR versions, and the replacement of "authorised employee" with "authorised bank employee or qualified electronic seal" — were **not re-confirmed this cycle** and should be treated as unverified.
date: 17/07/2026 — in force; compliance required now. The financial-inclusion bank package was adopted in June 2026 and the first licences are the forward trigger
implies: Ukraine has legalised agent-assisted and third-party-assisted verification with audio or video consent capture. That is a real fit for a digital-onboarding and e-signature stack — video identification, audio and video consent capture, qualified timestamping — delivered through tablets and kiosks at agent points rather than branches. Critically it creates a **new class of buyer that has never bought branch technology**: agent networks, post offices and retailers acting for a financial-inclusion bank, who need an onboarding device and eKYC software instead of a branch. The remediation-buy framing in the master row rested on the geotag claim and does not survive this cycle's re-reading.
likelihood: In force since 17/07/2026; agent-based and financial-inclusion-bank onboarding scales through 2026–2027 as licences are issued
follow_up: Obtain the consolidated text of Regulation No. 65 as amended and map the capture and consent requirements to the Namirial video-KYC flow. **Do not brief the geotag or unedited-photo requirement until it is found in the amended annex text** — two agents looked for it this cycle and neither found it. Track the first financial-inclusion bank licences and who supplies their agent-onboarding stack. Clear any biometric or photo-capture design with Printec's DPO before pitching.

bank_theme: NBU — AML enforcement biting at named banks, plus a published 2026 inspection calendar and an outsourcing-friendly monitoring rule
signal: Three strands converge into the cleanest dated compliance trigger in this market. **(1) Fines, published 07/08/2026** for July enforcement against 2 banks and 19 non-bank institutions: **JSC Raiffeisen Bank fined UAH 16,100,000** for improper customer due diligence, failure to apply a risk-based approach and risk-minimisation measures, failure to manage risks from new and existing information products, business practices or technologies including those enabling transactions without direct customer contact, late reporting of threshold transactions, and failure to supply the NBU with complete information — plus a written warning covering absent enhanced measures on politically exposed persons, **failure to configure and automate generation of the standard response forms in Annex 1 to Regulation No. 90**, failure to update customer questionnaires within 10 working days, and failure to transmit all received payer information on transfers. **JSC Bank Ukrainskyi Kapital fined UAH 42,545,000** in total, including the same automation failure and an inability to produce data to inspectors on time (A3, A4). **(2) A named, dated inspection calendar**: the NBU's plan as revised 31/07/2026 and updated 25/08/2026 lists Q1 Bank Ukrainskyi Kapital, Q2 Cominbank and UkrSibbank, Q3 Sky Bank and EPB, **Q4-2026 Asvio Bank, CB Globus and Bank KD** — and the chain is already proven, since the Q1 bank was fined in July (A3). **(3) A draft resolution on payment-service-provider control over payment operations** (consultation opened 17/07/2026, closed 14/08/2026, comments published 21/08/2026) sets single standardised approaches to monitoring and reconciliation of payment operations, and **explicitly provides for third parties to perform parts of the monitoring function** — that is regulatory permission to sell monitoring as a managed service — along with anti-miscoding measures and a prescribed list of signs of atypical user behaviour (A4). Related pressure at the top of the market: the NBU opened unscheduled inspections of Sense Bank on 21/08/2026 over alleged **interference with, and switching off of, the bank's automated systems** during transactions, stating that detection and suspension of suspicious transactions is the banks' own duty (A1).
date: 07/08/2026 — fines published against Raiffeisen Bank Ukraine and Bank Ukrainskyi Kapital. Forward: Q4-2026 on-site AML inspections at Asvio Bank, CB Globus and Bank KD, which must be briefed before end-September 2026
implies: The regulator is fining banks by name for precisely the things this software does — risk scoring, customer due diligence and profile data quality, PEP screening, threshold-transaction detection, payer-data completeness on transfers, and **failure to automate the regulator's own response forms**. Remediation follows NBU orders within one supervisory cycle, so budget commits immediately rather than at the next planning round. The published inspection calendar converts this from a general argument into three named accounts with a known deadline. And the draft monitoring resolution is rarer still: it licenses **outsourcing** the monitoring function, which is explicit permission to sell it as a managed service to providers that cannot staff a 24/7 desk.
likelihood: Very high — the NBU publishes enforcement monthly, the inspection plan is binding on the regulator, and remediation is mandatory
follow_up: Approach Raiffeisen Bank Ukraine on risk scoring, PEP screening and client-data remediation citing the 07/08/2026 findings, and brief Asvio Bank, CB Globus and Bank KD before end-September ahead of their Q4 inspections. Pull the August and September NBU enforcement notices. Read the comments file published 21/08/2026 on the monitoring draft — it names which providers pushed back and on what, which is a qualified prospect list — and track the adopted resolution and its transition period.

bank_theme: NBU Resolution No. 85 — TrekSEP payment-tracking duties, one-hour SLA already live
signal: A dated payments-instrumentation mandate that is **already binding, not a future deadline**. NBU Board Resolution **No. 85 of 05/08/2026, officially published 06/08/2026**, amends the Instruction on interbank payment operations in the national currency (Resolution No. 16 of 03/03/2023). It defines the **TrekSEP** message and service — an auxiliary information service allowing tracking of the stages of a SEP payment operation — and the concept of a SEP instant-transfer participant. **New point 46-4 obliges every SEP participant to send the payment-execution status to the SEP central processor as soon as possible and no later than ONE HOUR after that status is set in its own automation system and in the system of any non-bank provider settling through an account with that participant.** New point 46-5 obliges the participant to let the user query payment status remotely by sending a TrekSEP message, and to return the execution-stage information to the user through the remote channel. **Critical correction confirmed from the legal text:** point 4 of the resolution defers only paragraphs five to seven of sub-point 3 of point 1 — that is point 46-5 and its two sub-points **only** — to **01/01/2027**. Everything else, including the one-hour status-push duty in point 46-4, took effect the day after publication, i.e. **07/08/2026** (A3, A5). Context: SEP carries over 99% of Ukrainian interbank payments, is a designated systemically important RTGS running 24/7 on ISO 20022 since 01/04/2023, averages 1.5m payments a day worth about UAH 778bn, has offered instant credit transfer within 10 seconds since 01/12/2024, and SEP-4.2 with multi-currency support is under development; the NBU also states it is creating preconditions for eventual SEPA accession (A3).
date: 07/08/2026 — the one-hour status-push duty to the SEP central processor is already in force; the customer-facing TrekSEP query and status display follow on 01/01/2027
implies: Any Ukrainian bank or non-bank provider without end-to-end payment-status instrumentation is out of compliance **now**, and banks are expressly made responsible for the status data of the non-bank providers settling through their accounts — which most will not have wired up. Then by 01/01/2027 the same institutions must expose a status query and render the tracking stages in mobile and internet banking. The sequence is transaction instrumentation first and channel work second, and the "already binding" framing should move budget faster than a January date. The client-facing half is the part second-tier banks are least likely to have built.
likelihood: Very high — this is a published normative act and the entry-into-force dates were read directly from the text
follow_up: Request the TrekSEP message specification from the NBU Department of Payment Systems and Innovative Development. Open the conversation with second-tier banks now on how they plan to expose TrekSEP status in their channels before 01/01/2027. Confirm the paragraph-count reading of point 4 with Ukrainian counsel before telling any client it is already in breach.

bank_theme: NBU Resolutions No. 70, 72 and 73 — third-party risk management now binding on banks and payment providers
signal: A regime that cuts directly across Printec's own contracts and simultaneously creates demand. Three NBU Board Resolutions, **all dated 30/06/2026 and all in force from 01/07/2026**, install third-party-risk management across **banks and banking groups** (No. 70, amending the Regulation on the organisation of the risk-management system), **financial payment service providers** (No. 72) and **insurers** (No. 73). Confirmed requirements from the NBU's own notice: identification, assessment, control, monitoring and minimisation of third-party risks; **prior assessment of counterparties covering financial condition, business reputation and operational capability**; minimum contractual requirements; continuous monitoring of provider compliance; defined action where a provider or a critical provider falls short; business-continuity management taking third-party risk into account; **termination and exit plans**; and criteria for when a third-party relationship creates critical risk to continuity or to clients. The NBU says institutions have "sufficient time" to review existing supplier contracts but **publishes no transition date**. Legal basis is stated as Basel Committee recommendations, the payment services directive and Solvency II — **not** the IMF memorandum, PSD2 Article 20 or an EBA consultation paper, which were the basis previously assumed. Separately verified: NBU Resolution No. 143 of 09/12/2025 on organising information-security and cyber-protection measures by financial service providers exists and entered into force 13/12/2025, but **the widely-quoted "13/12/2026 transition end" could not be confirmed and is not stated on the NBU legislation page** (A3).

sources.text: NBU — third-party risk management requirements established

date: 01/07/2026 — in force for banks, payment service providers and insurers; contract re-papering is live now with no published transition deadline
implies: Every Ukrainian bank must now inventory, pre-assess and continuously monitor each critical technology supplier — **including ATM and recycler vendors and outsourced field-service providers** — and hold documented exit plans. This cuts both ways. It raises the due-diligence bar an incumbent supplier must clear, so Printec's own Ukrainian contracts need checking against the critical-contract criteria. It also creates budgeted demand for auditable device telemetry and monitoring, SLA-backed managed and field services, and documented continuity and exit evidence — the same compliance-grade wrapper Ukrgasbank has already started writing into its ATM service contracts.
likelihood: High — already in force since 01/07/2026, and re-papering of existing supplier contracts is under way
follow_up: Obtain the text of Resolution No. 70 from zakon.rada.gov.ua (the SSL handshake to that host failed this run) to extract any transition deadline for re-papering existing supplier contracts, and to confirm or kill the 13/12/2026 date attributed to Resolution No. 143 — **that date should not be quoted to a client until it is sourced**. Confirm whether Printec's Ukrainian contracts meet the NBU's critical-contract criteria before a bank's own review reaches them.

bank_theme: Ukraine open banking — ASPSP platform layer already delivered by a named incumbent
signal: **Reverse the master row's read.** The ASPSP-side build is not an opportunity being procured; it has been delivered. On **03/08/2026 the Open API HUB, via the EMA association, announced that OTP Bank, Sense Bank and Oschadbank had officially joined Ukraine's open-banking ecosystem, all three running Open API HUB's "API KIT" solution deployed on-premise inside each bank's own perimeter**, with Credit Agricole Bank and MTB Bank at final implementation stage (A1, A5). API KIT ships the full stack: a Berlin Group NextGenPSD2 / openFinance-based API specification, consent management, **third-party-provider verification against the NBU payment-infrastructure register with certificate validation**, an admin and monitoring platform with call logs and limits, a developer portal and dynamic sandbox, and a standardised core-banking connector. The regime itself is confirmed: NBU Board Resolutions **No. 80, 81 and 82 of 25/07/2025**, over Resolution No. 58 of 03/05/2023 on strong customer authentication and No. 43 of 19/05/2021 on information protection, with banks obliged to expose compliant account-information and payment-initiation APIs by **01/08/2026**, publish API technical documentation, and verify each provider's authorisation in real time before granting access (A1, A5). **The NBU's machine-readable register, pulled 31/08/2026, shows only three authorised institutions, all banks, all authorised in 2026 — PUMB from 02/03/2026, PrivatBank from 06/03/2026 and UkrSibbank from 01/05/2026 — giving exactly six active service entries, one payment-initiation and one account-information per bank. No non-bank third-party provider is yet authorised** (A6).

sources.text: EMA / Open API HUB — three banks live on API KIT

date: 03/08/2026 — Oschadbank, OTP Bank and Sense Bank went live on a competitor's platform; the 01/08/2026 statutory deadline has passed and the register was re-pulled 31/08/2026
implies: The API, consent, strong-authentication orchestration and certificate-verification work at the large Ukrainian banks is **sunk cost held by a named incumbent**, not a platform sale, and it should be dropped from the account plans. Three honest residual angles remain, all smaller and adjacent: HSM and key management sitting behind the on-premise deployments, API traffic security and fraud analytics on top of the new payment-initiation rail, and the mid-tier banks that have not gone live. The thin register is also useful negative evidence — with no non-bank provider authorised, the app-based disintermediation threat has not yet formed in Ukraine, so the near-term competitive pressure remains hardware, ATM service and cash automation.
likelihood: High that the API layer stays with the incumbent through 2027; medium that adjacent security and monitoring scope opens as account-information coverage widens
follow_up: Drop the ASPSP API build from the Oschadbank, OTP and Sense Bank plans. Instead ask Open API HUB and the banks who supplies the HSM and key management and the API-gateway security layer around API KIT, and whether payment-initiation transaction monitoring is in anyone's scope yet. Identify which mid-tier banks have **not** gone live — that shortlist, not the majors, is the addressable set. Re-pull the NBU register each cycle: the first non-bank authorisation marks a new competitor class.

bank_theme: Ukraine — flat ATM fleet against 96% cashless and continuing branch contraction
signal: The structural case is now backed by **exact counts from the NBU's own data file**, and the single most useful number has finally been published. From PC_table_1.xlsx at 01/07/2026: **15,768 ATMs, of which only 2,785 — 17.7% — are deposit-capable**, and that share has been flat since 2024 (2,624 at 01/01/2024, 2,754, 2,727, 2,785). Against that, **PTKS self-service payment kiosks grew 68% in a single year on a smooth monthly path, from 13,310 at 01/01/2025 to 22,376 at 01/01/2026 and 22,953 at 01/07/2026**; trade POS terminals reached 582,547 (+4.3% in six months) and card-accepting points 699,258 (+13.9%); softPOS tap-to-phone devices grew 65% to 69,783; and POS with cash-out reached 319,345 (A4). Cashless is **96% of card transactions by count but only 67% by value**, so roughly UAH 1.27tn still came out of the cash channel in H1-2026 across about 196m withdrawals; 153.2m cards are issued but only **61.1m active (40%), down from 65.4m in January** as state support programmes ended; 21.1m cards (34.5%) are tokenised and about 99% of in-store cashless transactions by both count and value are contactless (A1, A4). **Cash itself is not shrinking:** currency in circulation rose from UAH 759,753m (01/01/2025) to 866,943m (01/01/2026) to **921,808m at 01/08/2026 — +14.1% in 2025 and a further +6.3% in seven months** (A4). Branches: **4,754 operating structural units at 01/07/2026**, down 38 in the quarter and 5.1% since 01/01/2025, with **787 temporarily suspended** (Oschadbank 640, Raiffeisen 52, PrivatBank 2) (A1, A4). Raiffeisen Bank Ukraine is the sharpest case — 256 business outlets at 30/06/2026 against 295 a year earlier (-13.2%, the steepest cut in RBI outside Russia) while customers rose 8.2% to 3.124m (A1). The NBU's 2026 resilience assessment covers **26 named banks holding over 90% of system assets**, with results due by 31/12/2026 (A5).
date: 18/08/2026 — NBU H1-2026 card-market release and payment-infrastructure data file published; branch register and device counts as at 01/07/2026
implies: Rising note volumes handled by a flat ATM estate that is **only 17.7% deposit-capable** means rising cost per note handled and rising cash-in-transit dependency — the single strongest structural argument available in this market, and it is now a published fact rather than an inference. This is a **replacement and upgrade market, not a footprint market**: recyclers and teller cash recyclers to close the deposit gap, cash forecasting to cut replenishment runs, and back-office automation in the 4,754 remaining branches. The 68% kiosk boom makes kiosk hardware, software and managed services the fastest-growing physical channel in the country, and every one of those 22,953 devices is simultaneously a Resolution-67 software job and a UAH 2,000 note reconfiguration job. It sizes demand; it is not itself a procurement.
likelihood: Structural — the series is published monthly and every component moved in the same direction again this cycle
follow_up: Refresh PC_table_1.xlsx and the branch register each quarter — but note the NBU has flagged that the branch dataset will be **discontinued** in favour of the bank directory and the open-data API, so capture the API endpoint before the spreadsheet disappears. Pre-sales has to run in Q4-2026 and H1-2027 while the programme is being scoped, not when it is announced — and the decision sits with RBI group procurement in Vienna and the Zagreb integration office, not at Addiko. Sell service-shaped propositions to Addiko today and capital-shaped hardware to RBI. Note also that **NLB is left acquisitive with capital it earmarked for a deal it did not win**, which usually means another approach or accelerated organic investment.

bank_theme: Addiko carve-out to Alta Group — a six-bank Western Balkans group under a first-time owner
signal: **Serbia, both Bosnian banks and Montenegro do NOT go to Raiffeisen.** RBI keeps Croatia, Slovenia and Austria and will carve out the four Western Balkans banks — Addiko Bank AD Beograd, **Addiko Bank d.d. Sarajevo**, **Addiko Bank a.d. Banja Luka** and **Addiko Bank AD Podgorica** — selling them to **Alta Group d.o.o., Belgrade** (Serbian register no. 2103524), named in RBI's own offer document, which signed its transaction agreement with RBI on 08/05/2026. Alta is an NBS-licensed e-money institution that already owns Alta Banka AD Beograd and Alta Banka AD Bitola in North Macedonia and directly holds 9.63% of Addiko (A1, A5). **The dated clock that matters is not closing but the exit from shared services:** a Transitional Services Agreement runs **12 months after carve-out closing with a single 12-month extension**, after which the carved-out banks must source services from the buyer or from third parties — so replacements must be running roughly 2H2028 to 2H2029. Carve-out closing is expected H2-2027; Addiko's CEO said on 13/08/2026 that integration runs at least to end-2027 and probably into 2028. The equipment gaps are quantified from the banks' own published lists: **Addiko Sarajevo publishes 74 ATM locations of which only 25 accept cash, leaving 49 cash-out-only**; **Addiko Banja Luka operates just five cash-accepting ATMs** against roughly 45 cross-listed locations, despite already marketing a merchant cash-deposit flow and a 'Zona 24/7' deposit concept; neither BiH bank has any own POS estate. Addiko Serbia is the opposite — its product page states **every branch has an 'Addiko Express' dual-currency recycler** across 33 branches and 50 ATM locations. Montenegro is ~4% of group assets but has the group's best deposit build: 12 deposit-and-withdrawal machines across 18-19 ATM sites, the highest deposit share of any bank in the country, including coin acceptance and an SME daily-takings flow (A1). Alta is expanding fast beyond banking — it bought insurer ZOIL Makedonija, and in April 2026 Alta Retail took five Fortenova Serbia companies for ~EUR 140m, bringing roughly 300 Idea, Roda and Mercator stores. Sava Ivanov Dalbokov left the Addiko Group Supervisory Board on 31/07/2026 and joined Addiko Bank a.d. Beograd on 01/08/2026 as planned Chief Operating Officer, subject to NBS approval (A1, A5).
